It builds on ZSlayerHQ's victory-world-runtime with its own fixes for shaders, texture streaming and GPU memory. events.title: A public fork, VIctory-NVIDIA, reports 20 to 22 frames a second indoors and joins the table; VItoriaBr moves to 3rd
events.note: A public fork, VIctory-NVIDIA, reports 20 to 22 frames a second indoors and joins the table; VItoriaBr moves to 3rd  VIctory-NVIDIA, a fork of VIctory-7900XTX made to run on NVIDIA cards, joins the table at stage 6. Its README has reported since 23:46 UTC on 25 November about 20 to 22 rendered frames a second on average indoors in the opening on an RTX 5070 with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and 24 to 31 in lighter places. This page found it only now, through a fork of it that PortWatch's scout listed. The conditions matter: the smaller console's profile, the world drawn at 960 by 540 and upscaled, ray tracing mostly off, and its fastest settings, which leave some stretched bodies and miscoloured skin. One run each in the same PC measured 19.3 on the RTX 5070 and 14.9 on an RTX 5060 Ti, and a fork measured on an RTX 4060 Ti with a Ryzen 5 5600X, now on the watch list as VKarameloVI, reports 7 to 12. Its start script is set up for a driver feature that adds generated frames, and the figures here are its rendered frames. It gives no session length, so it is on the speed step the bar asks for and 3 steps short on stability, in 11th place. It is the first public code to report an average of 20 or more in play, and with PortWatch's report on the private build CGBJ it is the second report of that kind today. The estimate, moved earlier at 04:04 UTC , is held: it already assumed a build near 20. Also: VItoriaBr's README ( 04:09 UTC ) now documents 4 to 6 frames a second on its current settings

The code is private, so nobody outside the group can test it, and PortWatch's own notes say its graphics degraded as speed improved before the rating was raised. This page relays it as unconfirmed. CGBJ's speed lane now reads 25, the first row on the step the playable bar asks for. With no session length it is still 3 steps short and moves from 28th to 8th, and VIctory-7900XTX stays first. events.note: VIctory says only the frame rate keeps the game from working; Sixth Star joins the watch list  VIctory's README ( 23:27 UTC ) now heads its status with the frame rate as the one thing left: about 1 frame a second in the world on a Radeon RX 6700 XT, with the intro cutscene playing and the opening mission reached with the graphics fully displayed. Its figures and its place are unchanged; the faster figures on this page come from forks of its code. Sixth Star, a compatibility layer built from VIctory's code, joins the watch list at its maintainer's request. Its status file reports gameplay at about 5 frames a second on an RTX 3070 as its user's approximate observation, with stability not measured.     23:28  25 Nov

events.title: victory-fork now plays at 9 to 12 frames a second in light scenes, for half an hour at a time; VItoriaBr reports a process up for over two hours
events.note: victory-fork now plays at 9 to 12 frames a second in light scenes, for half an hour at a time; VItoriaBr reports a process up for over two hours  victory-fork's README ( 23:18 UTC ) now heads its status with play for half an hour at a time, slowly: about 9 to 12 frames a second in rooms and light outdoor views and 5 to 6 in heavy outdoor views. Its tester played from the opening past the first boat mission, and the graphics device was then lost in sessions of 6, 49 and 31 minutes, cause not known. This is the code most builds share. Its place is unchanged at 6th, two steps short: this page's playable bar asks for 20 frames a second. The README says the thread that prepares submissions is the limit, at about 70 milliseconds a frame plus 13 for every 1,000 draws. VItoriaBr's README gives one measured example of its process staying up for 2 hours 12 minutes, without saying what was played in that time. Read as its longest session, that lifts it from 22nd to 10th. News check: press coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond that notice, and GitHub's list has no new notice naming a project here. keylime's repository still does not answer.     23:05  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th
events.note: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th  Vice-Tay's README ( 21:32 UTC ) reports 30 minutes 12 seconds in the world without a crash on an RTX 4090, from a save in the opening mission with the player walking and turning the camera throughout. The median over the session was 7.0 frames a second, 6.3 to 9.5 by stretch and 1.9 to 3.8 through one scene change. Its maintainer ended it by choice because memory grows by about 1 GB a minute. The row moves from 17th to 6th. VIctory's main branch took its first commits since 16:51 UTC : five merges between 21:35 and 21:40 UTC . Its README still gives about 1 frame a second. victory-fork's README ( 21:28 UTC ) says that with its new water read-back a tester's run got past a point where a mission had failed at once, then lost the graphics card for a reason not known. BRVIctory-ka1qux now gives about 3 frames a second on its street with ray-traced light and no longer lists the 6.6 to 6.9 it had reported from an earlier build.     21:26  25 Nov

events.title: AnyXboxX gives a session length and edges back to first; victory-fork reports 49 minutes of play; keylime's repository stops answering
events.note: AnyXboxX gives a session length and edges back to first; victory-fork reports 49 minutes of play; keylime's repository stops answering  AnyXboxX's README ( 22:54 UTC ) now gives a length for its figure: automated 13-minute runs on an RTX 4070 SUPER at a median of 13.8 frames a second in the world, 15.6 to 17 over the last minute, without a crash, up from 10.9 with its earlier settings. That puts the middle of its reported range just above VIctory-7900XTX's, so the two swap places, each one step short of the playable bar. victory-fork's README ( 22:50 UTC ) reports a 49-minute play session that ended when the graphics device was lost, and a later run it calls the best so far, with the water right and boats floating. It measured that nearly all of the memory it copies back from the card is read by nothing, and names that as the next thing to cut. keylime's repository stopped answering between 22:28 and 22:59 UTC : missing, private or removed. No takedown notice names it and the reason is not known. GitHub's notice list gained one entry, about an unrelated library. klbf-lab removed the names of the game, its characters and its missions from its README. vilocity reports faces lit in the opening cutscenes and a median frame of 222 milliseconds in its latest run. The estimate is unchanged: neither published mark is met.     22:39  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: VIctory-7900XTX is published with 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and goes first; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
events.note: VIctory-7900XTX is published with 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and goes first; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier  VIctory-7900XTX, a fork of VIctory whose README went up at 22:14 UTC , reports 13 to 20 frames a second indoors in the opening, 19 to 22 on the first boat mission and 6 to 10 in a busy street chase on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX at 1440p, with a longest session of 41 minutes without a crash. It gives no average for a whole session and lists flicker on trees and far buildings. PortWatch's owner says it verified the build at about 16 on average; it is one machine and nobody else has reproduced it. It enters at stage 6 in first place, one step short of the playable bar, ahead of AnyXboxX on the middle of its reported range. The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, on the mark published at 21:26 UTC , with the caveats set out in the revision note. A reader posted a 12-minute run of AnyXboxX on an RTX 4090 to this page's issues: a median of 2 frames a second in the world, rising to about 7 in its last two minutes, against the README's 12.5 on another card. The page has not verified it. AnyXboxX's speed is now marked unconfirmed, and its place still follows its own report. Vertex, a fork of VIctory measured on an RTX 5070 with 12 GB, joins at stage 6 at its maintainer's request: a median of 6.4 to 9.9 frames a second by run and a longest session of 25 minutes. Victory-United, a tree that gathers

events.title: VIctory merges about 70 pull requests into its main branch, vilocity clears its last orange marks and VIniVIdiVIci confirms control
events.note: VIctory merges about 70 pull requests into its main branch, vilocity clears its last orange marks and VIniVIdiVIci confirms control  VIctory's main branch took 74 commits between 21:35 and 21:57 UTC , its first since 16:51 UTC , among them the drawing of the interface planes the game uses on the smaller console's profile. Its README's status is unchanged at about 1 frame a second. vilocity's README ( 21:46 UTC ) says the last orange marks are gone, with window light and shadows now falling on heads. Its latest test run shows a median frame of 339 milliseconds, about 3 frames a second, where earlier runs showed about 130. VIniVIdiVIci's README ( 21:48 UTC ) says player control is confirmed with scripted input and nobody at the keyboard: the camera turned, the character moved and the pause menu opened. AnyXboxX has not yet given a session length for its figure of about 12 frames a second.     21:48  25 Nov

events.title: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th
events.note: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th  Vice-Tay's README ( 21:32 UTC ) reports 30 minutes 12 seconds in the world without a crash on an RTX 4090, from a save in the opening mission with the player walking and turning the camera throughout. The median over the session was 7.0 frames a second, 6.3 to 9.5 by stretch and 1.9 to 3.8 through one scene change. Its maintainer ended it by choice because memory grows by about 1 GB a minute. The row moves from 17th to 6th. VIctory's main branch took its first commits since 16:51 UTC : five merges between 21:35 and 21:40 UTC . Its README still gives about 1 frame a second. victory-fork's README ( 21:28 UTC ) says that with its new water read-back a tester's run got past a point where a mission had failed at once, then lost the graphics card for a reason not known. BRVIctory-ka1qux now gives about 3 frames a second on its street with ray-traced light and no longer lists the 6.6 to 6.9 it had reported from an earlier build. events.note: AnyXboxX reports about 12 frames a second on a new base and takes first place, and the estimate moves to early Friday  AnyXboxX's README ( 20:50 UTC ) says its maintainer measured a median of 12.5 frames a second in the world on an RTX 4070 SUPER at 4K output, about 15 over the last minute with peaks at 30 and no crash, after moving its code to a base it calls Neptune: a packaged edition of VIctory, shipped with its source, whose author it says has no public contact. Its previous base ran at about 5 there. The README does not say how long the session ran, and the figures are its own, from one machine. By the rule AnyXboxX is now first, 1 step short of the playable bar. Its speed lane reads the new base; its stability lane is still a contributor's relayed 45 minutes on the earlier base, and the row says so. Kelvaroq is second. Kelvaroq's README now cites its place on this page and carries a banner for the AI product it is built with. The tester behind its 36-minute session is not named, nobody else has confirmed the session, and PortWatch does not track Kelvaroq as a separate effort because it reads its results as VIctory's and victory-fork's code. A place here is computed from what a project reports about itself and is not a verification; the Positions note now says so. events.title: Kelvaroq takes first place: an outside tester's 36 minutes at about 10 frames a second on an RTX 4090
events.note: Kelvaroq takes first place: an outside tester's 36 minutes at about 10 frames a second on an RTX 4090  Kelvaroq's README ( 20:53 UTC ) records an outside tester's session of 36 minutes 46 seconds without a crash on an RTX 4090, through the opening mission and the next. It averaged 10 frames a second over the whole session and 10.9 after the first ten minutes, which the README describes as loading with dips to 1. It is one session, and the README says its monitor was restarted once. That gives Kelvaroq a session length where it had only 5-minute runs. It is now 2 steps short of the playable bar and takes first place from klbf-lab by the rule: the same picture step and a higher frame rate. It is the best average yet from a session of 20 minutes or more, and the first of Kelvaroq's figures from a second machine. The estimate is unchanged for now. This is the session averaging 10 or more that the published mark for moving later asked for by 12:00 UTC on 26 November , so that mark no longer applies. The mark for moving earlier asks for 12, and playable needs 20. Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 8 frames a second, with 7.2 to 7.7 standing still, and a stand-in light that follows the game's sky. Vice-Tay's README says its current build, rebuilt on VIctory's code, ran the opening cutscene at a median of 0.8 frames a second, and that its 4.3 to 7.5 came from an earlier revision.     20:40  25 Nov

The build joins the table as a private row in 11th place with every figure marked as relayed. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, the code is not public, no session length is given, and nothing says whether the counter shows rendered frames. PortWatch's pinned notes since then ask the streamer to release the code. A news sweep at 20:16 UTC found no second source for that build. Coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, no notice names another project, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked. A small Manifold market, with four traders, gives about 1 in 5 that GitHub publishes a Take-Two notice naming VIctory by the end of the year. Vice-Tay's maintainer confirmed the move from victory-windows in a request on this page's repository and says the length of its test sessions is unknown. victory-perf's repository still does not answer. The estimate is unchanged. A reading of a stream is not the measured session of 10 minutes or more, averaging 12 or more in rendered frames, that the published mark asks for. events.title: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar
events.note: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar  PortWatch removed omonkey from its board at 18:19 UTC , saying on its owner's word that the private build has been taken down. Its code was never public, so there is nothing to check, and no notice or statement has been published. VGTimes reported earlier today that its developer reported receiving a letter from Rockstar and stopped streaming. Its row here keeps its last reported status. With ztrx's repository and account gone since about 17:00 UTC , two builds of victory-fork's code have gone dark today with no reason published. The mark published with the estimate asks for a takedown notice that names VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, and GitHub's list holds none, so the estimate is unchanged. Both cases will weigh in its next review. vilocity's README now gives 4 to 8 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 3 to 7. klbf-lab's README adds that it never publishes a build that crashed in its own tests and that its 77-minute session was stopped by choice. XCL merged 28 pull requests into its main branch with its status row unchanged.     18:13  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held
events.note: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held  ztrx's repository has not answered since 16:57 UTC , in three checks over 25 minutes while every other tracked repository answered, the last of them after GitHub closed its incident at 16:52 UTC . GitHub's published list holds no notice that names it and PortWatch still lists it, so the reason is not known: a repository made private, deleted or disabled looks the same from outside. Its row keeps its last reported status, without a link. Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 7 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, from 3 to 5: 5.4 to 6.7 standing still in a scene of 8,400 draws, less while driving. Its README puts the gain down to letting the game's submissions return before the card is done and to using game memory in place instead of copying it. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it rises to 4th. BRVIctory-ka1qux has turned the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the first public build on this page to do so. Its README says it costs 0.05 to 0.1 seconds a frame and has been checked on one open-world street only, in four runs of 5 to 11 minutes without a crash. The estimate was reviewed at 17:24 UTC and held at about a day. events.title: A private build's developer reports a letter from Rockstar, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second
events.note: A private build's developer reports a letter from Rockstar, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second  VGTimes reports that the developer of the private build listed here as omonkey reports receiving a letter from Rockstar and has stopped streaming the work, while promising further updates. The letter has not been published and Rockstar has not commented. It is the first report of this kind seen here. Flamingo's run log reports a 24-minute play session through the whole opening and on into the city, at 8.6 frames a second on average in the world on an RTX 4070. That is the highest average reported from a session of 20 minutes or more, from one machine and unconfirmed, and it is under the 10 the next mark asks for. An open pull request against victory-fork reports the game's ray-tracing structure builder running whole through 7 minutes of play, kept off by default because it costs about 88 milliseconds a frame. VIniVIdiVIci moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5: its README reports the world at 3 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 4060 Ti, with no input tested yet. Forecast review: the estimate stays at the evening of Thu 26 Nov. The afternoon has brought more builds, a session from a new game into the open world and ray tracing as an experiment, but no figure above 14 in play, and victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC . News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no notice naming another project.     15:13  25 Nov

events.title: victory-unified reports 58 minutes without a crash, and PortWatch says the private stream build runs on VIctory's code
events.note: victory-unified reports 58 minutes without a crash, and PortWatch says the private stream build runs on VIctory's code  victory-unified's README ( 20:38 UTC ) reports about 58 minutes in one session with no crash on an RTX 3070 with 8 GB, from the opening into a later mission outdoors, at 2 to 3 frames a second. It follows a fix for the graphics-device failure that ended its two earlier sessions at about 49 minutes. PortWatch added at 20:30 UTC , on its owner's word, that darkworldhm builds on a fork of VIctory, which one is not known. The build is still self-reported and its figures are still a reading of a live stream; its row here says so. VIniVIdiVIci reports four sessions of ten minutes that ran to their time limit without a crash with a texture change for 8 GB cards. There is no commit at victory-fork since 19:39 UTC or on VIctory's main branch since 16:51 UTC , and victory-perf's repository still does not answer.     20:19  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed
events.note: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed  PortWatch's entry for darkworldhm stood for a round and was raised at 19:59 UTC : its owner now reports free roam at 5 to 24 frames a second on the stream, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading. The build joins the table as a private row in 11th place with every figure marked as relayed. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, the code is not public, no session length is given, and nothing says whether the counter shows rendered frames. PortWatch's pinned notes since then ask the streamer to release the code. A news sweep at 20:16 UTC found no second source for that build. Coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, no notice names another project, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked. A small Manifold market, with four traders, gives about 1 in 5 that GitHub publishes a Take-Two notice naming VIctory by the end of the year. Vice-Tay's maintainer confirmed the move from victory-windows in a request on this page's repository and says the length of its test sessions is unknown. victory-perf's repository still does not answer. The estimate is unchanged. A reading of a stream is not the measured session of 10 minutes or more, averaging 12 or more in rendered frames, that the published mark asks for.     19:57  25 Nov

events.note: PortWatch now reports a private build at about 12 frames a second in free roam, ruff-lab reaches stage 6, and the estimate is held  PortWatch replaced its pinned note at 19:42 UTC : its owner now reports a private build, darkworldhm, shown on a live stream in free roam at 5 to 18 frames a second, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading, reportedly on an RTX 50-series card. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, its code is not public, what it builds on is not known, and nothing says whether the figure counts rendered frames only. This page waits one round, or for a second source, before giving a private build a row. ruff-lab moves to stage 6: its README now reports the player in control with a DualShock 4 on a Radeon RX 6600 XT with 8 GB, 16 GB of memory and a hard disk, in a 39-minute session without a crash at 3.6 frames a second on average. victory-fork's README ( 19:39 UTC ) now heads its status with 8 to 10 frames a second in the first rooms and 5 to 8.5 through the opening cutscene, measured with changes that are off by default, and its evening code is in the tree with no speed gain shown. victory-windows is now published as Vice-Tay by the same maintainer, and victory-perf's repository still does not answer. events.title: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering
events.note: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering  victory-fork's README ( 19:21 UTC ) claims no frame-rate gain and says its headline figures stand. A frame capture now built into the layer puts the card's time for the game's own commands at 15 to 25 milliseconds a frame in the opening cutscene, far less than a whole frame, and the project says the time taken by the layer's own work does not add up yet. Keeping part of the game's memory copies on the graphics card cut the time spent in frames longer than 250 milliseconds from 21 and 26% to 4 and 6% in the opening cutscene, in two launches each way. The project calls it a result, not yet a default, and reports two other changes that measured no gain and were dropped. It also says a review of the open pull requests for frame rate found no single large gain, and that the change it had listed as the large step would be a modest one on its test PC. victory-perf's repository stopped answering over git between 18:56 and 19:28 UTC : missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. It is the third build of victory-fork's code to become unavailable today, after ztrx and the private build omonkey, and a news sweep at 19:27 UTC found no report about it. Two more forks join the watch list: VIctory-forkAMD and HybridGt.      See 134 earlier updates    19:05  25 Nov

events.title: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering
events.note: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering  victory-fork's README ( 19:21 UTC ) claims no frame-rate gain and says its headline figures stand. A frame capture now built into the layer puts the card's time for the game's own commands at 15 to 25 milliseconds a frame in the opening cutscene, far less than a whole frame, and the project says the time taken by the layer's own work does not add up yet. Keeping part of the game's memory copies on the graphics card cut the time spent in frames longer than 250 milliseconds from 21 and 26% to 4 and 6% in the opening cutscene, in two launches each way. The project calls it a result, not yet a default, and reports two other changes that measured no gain and were dropped. It also says a review of the open pull requests for frame rate found no single large gain, and that the change it had listed as the large step would be a modest one on its test PC. victory-perf's repository stopped answering over git between 18:56 and 19:28 UTC : missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. It is the third build of victory-fork's code to become unavailable today, after ztrx and the private build omonkey, and a news sweep at 19:27 UTC found no report about it. Two more forks join the watch list: VIctory-forkAMD and HybridGt.     19:05  25 Nov

events.title: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days
events.note: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days  victory-fork's README ( 17:28 UTC ) reports a 370-second play session at 4.5 frames a second on average, against 10.3 standing still. Half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle, because the game maps every streamed texture page itself, about 850 pages in a frame that streams. Two attempts to cut that cost were taken back out, one after faces came out black or red. events.title: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment
events.note: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment  VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README (14:00 UTC) says its stand-in for ray-traced light is now weaker in creases and under objects, and that the game's own sun and lamp shadows work. It still reports 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, says about 380 draws a frame are dropped, and says the frame is bound by the processor's work. VIctory-macOS reports its current code staying in the world for over 20 minutes without freezing on an M3 Max, at 0.1 to 0.2 frames a second. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac. News check: IGN has reported on the takedown and says it has asked Take-Two for comment. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project. VIniVIdiVIci, a fork of victory-fork checked on an RTX 4060 Ti, joins the watch list at a reader's request. Its README says it has not yet published results of its own in play. The estimate is unchanged at the evening of Thu 26 Nov.     14:01  25 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: klbf-lab plays the second mission to its end, two forks join the table, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
events.note: klbf-lab plays the second mission to its end, two forks join the table, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier  klbf-lab's README (13:47 UTC) reports the opening mission and all of the second played to the end in one 77-minute session without a crash on its newest test build, on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, at about 5.2 frames a second on average and about 9 in flight. It says the game's own saves work, and that vegetation turns magenta and the ground stays very dark at night. Two forks of victory-fork join the table at stage 6, on their READMEs' own figures from one machine each. Flamingo reports the first gameplay scene of a title it does not name at 9 to 12 frames a second on an RTX 4070 at reduced resolution, about 14 in its lightest view, in 15-minute runs, and enters second in the order. BRVIctory-ka1qux reports a 25-minute play session and 6.6 to 6.9 in steady open-world views on a Radeon RX 7800 XT. The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to the evening of Thu 26 Nov, just over a day away. Flamingo's is the second report of 10 or more in play, from a second machine after victory-perf's, which is the condition this page published at 10:36 UTC. Both come from the lightest scenes, Flamingo's newest code is at 9 to 10, and ordinary play elsewhere is 5 to 9 against the 20 the bar asks for, so the move is small. What moves it next. It has not yet played that mission to its end on the build. events.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
events.note: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first  Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count. Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3. The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. A project that reports no run length counts as having none, which is why VItoriaBr and ScarlettPort sit lower than before. The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. Stages below 6 have no lanes and are still ordered by this page's reading.      See 118 earlier updates    13:04  25 Nov

events.title: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8
events.note: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8  At 12:20 UTC this page reported victory-fork's first room at 6.0 frames a second by default and 8.9 with a newer draw path. events.title: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days
events.note: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days  victory-fork's maintainer merged texture fixes at 03:19 UTC, the first change to its main branch in two hours. The notes say the first room now shows its walls and the characters' textures on a first launch, and put speed at about 3 to 5 frames a second. They add that more than half of the card's texture memory is held for detail levels the game has not loaded, which is the next job. Routine review of the estimate at 03:30 UTC: unchanged at about 2 days. Stability has three reports beyond the bar, so speed is the gap. The best measured figure in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over five hours, most of them overnight in Europe, while more than 500 pull requests have now been opened against the fork. That is too short a pause to move the estimate later, and nothing has happened to move it earlier. One clue on speed for common cards: an open pull request on the fork measures the graphics time per frame in the first room at about three times higher on an 8 GB card once its texture memory runs out. Press: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared in any coverage found. The Verge reported the Leonida takedown on 24 November, and by Make Tech Easier's account it names VIctory and its forks as the projects in front. Notebookcheck relays unverified Reddit claims that more Discord servers have been removed.     03:10  25 Nov

An open pull request against victory-fork reports all 52 programs of the game's ray-tracing structure builder translating on an RTX 3060 laptop card, up from 49. Its author says the builder then writes outside its buffers and the game faults, so ray-traced lighting is still missing. PortWatch now ranks ztrx first on its board, saying the build has not crashed between the opening mission and the second. Speed is unchanged everywhere: about 7.6 frames a second at best in play.     02:49  25 Nov

It joins at stage 5, in sixth place. five-star-recomp now runs for three minutes without a crash, with real images on screen, while the game is still loading. A community project list reports that a second, smaller project, americas-recomp, went offline on 23 November shortly before Leonida. No cause is given for either.     02:35  24 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: Xbox2Windows reports a visible intro
events.note: Xbox2Windows reports a visible intro  Xbox2Windows: a contributor reports a visible intro video on an RX 9070 XT, with wrong colours and black frames after it. The project moves from stage 3 to stage 5, in sixth place, and has not yet checked a frame against a reference. five-star-recomp is past the assert that stopped it and now streams the game's next stage, compressed textures included. It stops at one texture layout method it has not implemented yet. Six projects now show a picture from the game. None has drawn the world.     01:58  24 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及画面输出；不代表完整图形管线或可玩性已解决。

events.title: Estimate moves back a day
events.note: Estimate moves back a day  The best estimate to playable moves from about 3 days to about 4, around Sat 28 Nov. Nobody has drawn the world in the three and a half hours since the first project got inside it, and frame times there are ten times or more too slow. Palmwave now loads the world at 5 to 30 frames a second with memory levelling off. It stops as the world starts to draw, when the game's watchdog ends a wait for pipelines still compiling. five-star-recomp added a disk pipeline cache. VIctory and XCL's main branch have had no substantive change for about two hours. Press coverage has started: outlets report the game reaching its settings and legal screens on PC, with nothing playable.     01:38  24 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: Two of Leonida's forks are gone

The cause is not known, and no takedown notice naming the project has been published. five-star-recomp's first image now shows in the right colours after a fix to 61 pipelines. No project changed stage.     01:19  24 Nov

XCL merged a change that skips uploading textures whose memory has not changed. Its status line is unchanged. Five projects now show a picture from the game. events.title: Three more projects report start-up progress
events.note: Three more projects report start-up progress  Palmwave, a fork of XCL, measures a retail game it does not name into world loading on an RTX 5080: 0 to 2 frames a second, with memory growing until the run is stopped at 140 seconds. It joins the standings in third. Its own fix lifts the intro video from 3.5 to about 19 frames a second. It reports that compressed world textures are not decoded yet in this code. Xbox2Windows says local runs of the main executable now reach graphics pipeline creation, its first report of running the title's own code. No rendered frame is verified. Holy-Interoperability presents its first frame of a retail title it does not name, then stops in start-up.     00:39  24 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及画面输出；不代表完整图形管线或可玩性已解决。

events.title: XCL's code is measured on a second PC
events.note: XCL's code is measured on a second PC  Palmwave, now built on XCL's code, measured a retail game it does not name on an RTX 5080. It shows first screens at up to 30 frames a second, slows to about 3 frames a second, then crashes as memory grows while the world loads. Its list of what separates that code from playable: memory growth in world loading, which XCL has since fixed, texture decoding failures, refused mesh pipelines and a slow phase with no known cause. TuxBox: shader preparation now compiles 2,755 of 11,429 requests captured from its runs. Its picture is unchanged at the player-selection prompt. VIctory merged 11 fixes from outside contributors in half an hour. Its status is unchanged.     00:19  24 Nov
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: VIctory draws the first mission's title card
events.note: VIctory draws the first mission's title card  VIctory: after the world loads, the first mission's title card now renders. It is the first picture past the loading screen that any project on this page has reported. The scene after the card is still dark, at 0.5 to 1.8 seconds a frame, and runs end on a graphics fault within about 55 seconds. five-star-recomp: the game now reads input, starts its save system and pairs a gamepad after a scripted button press. Frames are still black, and an assert inside the game stops it there. Palmwave has switched to XCL's code. XCL's own status line is unchanged, and Leonida is still unreachable.     23:56  23 Nov

events.title: Leonida halts: its lead steps away and its repository is gone
events.note: Leonida halts: its lead steps away and its repository is gone  Leonida's lead posted that he is stepping away. GitHub shows a notice page for repositories removed on a copyright complaint and has published none; contributors' forks and the lead's other repository are still up. The projects ahead of it are unaffected: VIctory, XCL, TuxBox and five-star-recomp were all reachable at 23:56 UTC.     23:54  23 Nov

events.title: ZETTROX's GTA VI build looks uncrashable so far
events.note: ['ZETTROX\'s build of GTA VI hasn\'t crashed yet. It has played from Lucia\'s prologue into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing", where it showed the first kill with a gun in GTA VI on PC, and it hasn\'t gone down once along the way. Its README reports more than an hour and a half in one session without a crash.', 'That\'s rare this early. Running a game built for other hardware usually means crashing, and often. ZETTROX\'s is the only build on our board rated better than "Crashes sometimes": on Wednesday its stability went from 0.5 to 0.8 ("Rarely crashes"), which puts it first at 64.2%.', "It's also slowly getting toward free roam, the point where the story lets go and the open world is yours. That takes patience: the build runs at 1 to 3 frames per second, and the picture is still poor, with anything in shadow drawn black and bright scenes overexposed.", "What keeps it running isn't clear yet. Like Uilian's VItoriaBr, it's based on VIctory and hyphennn's victory-fork, with ZETTROX's own work for NVIDIA cards, tested on an RTX 3050. Unlike most builds this far along, its code is public, as Zettrox/ztrx, so anyone can compare it with victory-fork and find what's different."]
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: GTA VI builds clear Lucia's prologue and reach Jason's first mission
events.note: ['Several private PC builds of GTA VI can now play through Lucia\'s prologue and carry on into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing". Until now, the furthest builds we track had only reached the prologue itself, so this is the deepest into the story anyone has reported.', "It's rough. Most builds still render the world badly, and vehicles don't work most of the time: in Gone Fishing the boat often can't be steered. On some builds, the map in the pause menu opens.", "We can't say yet whose builds these are. The people getting this far are working in private, and most of them appear to build on hyphennn's victory-fork, the public fork of VIctory behind the top of our board. Their own changes aren't public, so nobody else can test them.", '"Prologue cleared" is the first step of our story track, but no score changes until we know which builds did it. If yours is one of them, open an issue on our GitHub with a link to a recording or a stream.']

events.title: We've seen Belobug's AMD build, and it's way ahead
events.note: ["We've seen Belobug's build of GTA VI running, and the PortWatch team thinks it's way ahead of every other build we track. The open world renders lit, with textures, people, vehicles, vegetation, water and sky, and it looks close to the retail game, just very slowly. It plays through missions, and it rarely crashes.", 'It went straight to #1 on our board at 77.4%, more than 13 points clear of ZETTROX\'s 64.2%, which led until this morning. Its rendering is rated 0.85 on our scale, the highest we\'ve given any build, and its story progress 0.5 ("First act"). The next best picture, suri\'s private build, is at 0.8; ZETTROX\'s, which draws anything in shadow black, is at 0.3.', "It's built for AMD Radeon, while ZETTROX's, the previous leader, is tuned for NVIDIA. Belobug runs it on a Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB of RAM and Windows 11. It's a fork of Marvis's VIctory, following its main branch plus upstream pull requests, and its README says no code from hyphennn's victory-fork is in it. Belobug's own fixes include a stand-in for the game's ray-traced indirect light, which left leaves magenta and indoor scenes in coloured blocks, a fix for lines along every triangle on car paint, glass and skin, and a change that cut the GPU time of one heavy scene from 225 to about 80 milliseconds a frame.", 'It isn\'t fast. events.title: Take-Two's first GTA VI port takedown disables Leonida and 3,007 forks
events.note: ['Take-Two has filed its first DMCA notice against a GTA VI port. The notice, published in GitHub\'s public DMCA log on Tuesday, names ItsNotRexed\'s Leonida repository. Because the fork network was larger than 100 repositories and Take-Two said the forks infringe just as the original does, GitHub processed it against the whole network: 3,007 repositories. Contributor forks that survived Leonida\'s shutdown on Monday now show GitHub\'s "unavailable" page.', 'The publisher calls Leonida a derivative work of GTA VI and says it breaches the reverse-engineering ban in Rockstar\'s terms of service. It also argues that the project\'s "bring your own files" line is misleading: given the timing, it says, the files users must supply can only be the leaked Xbox build.', "The notice names only Leonida. Projects that aren't GitHub forks of it, such as VIctory and XCL, and Leonida copies uploaded as new repositories, are still online for now. But the same argument could apply to any of them.", 'Leonida stays on our board as nuked, for the record.']
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: PortWatch's new scale: Playable is halfway, finishing the game is 100%
events.note: ['We\'ve changed how PortWatch scores projects. The old bar climbed from groundwork to "In-game", then to 30 FPS and "Stable". Many of you pointed out that this mixed up two different things: getting the game to run at all, and having it play well. Walking around a dark world at 5 frames per second isn\'t three-quarters of the way to playing GTA VI on PC.', 'Getting in is now a ladder to 50%. Groundwork fills the first 10%. Then come Exe runs (10%), First frame (20%), Main menu (30%), In the world (40%), when story mode loads the world and draws it, however broken, and Playable (50%), when you control a character in it.', 'Past Playable, four tracks fill the other half side by side: story progress (35 points), from stuck in the opening to 100% completion; rendering (25), from black or broken to matching the console; performance (20), the average frame rate divided by 30; and stability (20). 100% now means the whole game can be finished, looking like the console, at 30 fps or better, without crashing.', "Every project has been re-scored, and the numbers are lower. The furthest builds are now just past halfway: hyphennn's private build at 59.4%, omonkey's at 57.9%, victory-gta6 at 57.3% and CGBJ's at 54.5%. VIctory is at 40%, in the world but not yet playable, and XCL at 35%. Nobody went backwards: the same results now count for less of the whole game.", 'The history chart has been converted to the new scale too. events.title: Exclusive: CGBJ gets GTA VI in game, walking and talking in an unlit world
events.note: ['A group called CGBJ has got GTA VI into its game world on PC, and a player can move in it. With a controller they walk around, talk to NPCs and open the in-game menu. PortWatch has verified that it gets in game. No public project has shown a player moving yet.', "It is far from playable, and it runs very slowly. In the run where a player walked around, the screen was black. A 77-second video posted on X on Tuesday shows more: GTA VI's opening scenes in flat colours with no lighting, from a car's interior to a street of waving NPCs, a guard and a prison yard.", "CGBJ's code is private. It builds on VIctory, the open-source layer whose author first showed GTA VI's menus on a livestream on Monday, and also takes some of XCL's work. Both are public on GitHub; CGBJ's changes aren't, so nobody outside the group can test them.", "We've added CGBJ to the tracker at 72%, at our In-game stage, which puts it first. That rests on our own check: the video doesn't name the project, and nobody outside the group can reproduce the result yet.", "Update, 20:10 UTC: our race now ranks only projects with public code, so CGBJ's private build is listed below it without a rank, still at 72%. It counts toward our overall progress number, which omonkey's private build now leads at 76%, and it shows on the cards of VIctory and XCL as a build on their code."]

events.title: Exclusive: XCL reports 30 fps in GTA VI but won't say if it's past the menus
events.note: ["XCL says GTA VI now runs at 30 frames per second in game, but won't say where. Asked whether that means the menus it had already reached or actual gameplay, the team refused to answer, saying it feared being nuked. Privately, it hinted to one of our community members that things are working really well.", 'Its public notes haven\'t caught up. XCL\'s README still calls the game "a newer retail game" that reaches its menus at a steady 30 fps, with gameplay not reached yet. Early on Tuesday the project merged a change that shows the live frame rate in the game window\'s title.', "The caution runs through the scene. XCL's Discord server is tightly locked down with its chats closed, and members are scared of being nuked after Leonida lost its server, its repository and its creator within an hour on Monday night. The GTA 6 Modding Discord server has now been nuked too.", 'Update, 01:50 UTC: testers on XCL\'s GitHub now report GTA VI getting past its menus into the world on the public code. The game\'s own state reads "Game Running", but the screen stays on a loading spinner and a GPU watchdog ends each run within minutes. One report claims gameplay at 28 to 30 fps, without a screenshot. XCL moves to 62.5%, halfway to In-game.']

events.title: TuxBox draws GTA VI's first screen as VIctory edges into the world
events.note: ["Leonida's exit hasn't slowed the other GTA VI ports. TuxBox, a compatibility layer tested mostly on Linux through Proton, published a run record showing the game's player-selection prompt at 4K on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. It hasn't sent the game any input yet, so we count it as a first frame, not a menu. That takes TuxBox from 25% to 40%.", "VIctory, level with XCL at the main menu, now says its runs reach the world. The first mission's title card renders, but the scene behind it stays dark at roughly one frame every one to two seconds, and the project warns that real GPUs can hang. That isn't playable, so VIctory stays at 55%.", 'PercyScarlett reports GTA VI running to a frame loop of black frames before the GPU hangs, and a new project, GTA6-BootTest, gets its exe through the same stage with stand-in DLLs. Both now sit at "Exe runs". As always, these are the projects\' own reports; none has been reproduced independently.']

events.title: Leonida is nuked: GitHub repo deleted, Discord gone, creator quits
events.note: ['Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port with more than 33,000 GitHub stars, went offline in under an hour on Monday night. Its Discord server stopped resolving at about 23:07 UTC. By 23:47 its GitHub repository was gone. Around the same time its creator, NotRexed, posted "I quit guys" on X, writing that he kept running into problems he couldn\'t control and was stepping away, and thanking the Discord community.', 'The repository now answers "not found", not the "unavailable" page GitHub shows after a DMCA takedown, and GitHub\'s public DMCA log has no notice against it. That points to its owners pulling it rather than Take-Two, though only they can say. Earlier that evening it had moved to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, whose maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues.', "The code isn't lost. Contributors' forks are still on GitHub, among them the one carrying the combined boot fixes, and a mirror on NotRexed's own Git server holds the code as of 23:30 UTC, though it can no longer sync.", "We've marked Leonida as nuked on the tracker. It stays on the board for the record but no longer counts in the rankings.", "Update, Nov 24: Take-Two has since filed a DMCA notice against Leonida, published in GitHub's log on Nov 24, and GitHub disabled the repository's whole network of 3,007 forks, including the contributor fork linked below. Copies uploaded as separate repositories are not part of that network."]
events.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

events.title: Leonida's Discord server disappears as the project moves to a new GitHub account
events.note: ["Leonida's Discord server went offline late on Monday. At 23:06 UTC its invite still led to a server of about 179,000 members, 74,000 of them online. Within a minute Discord answered that both the invite and the server were unknown. Members say Discord banned it. Neither Discord nor the Leonida team has said why, and from outside we can't tell a ban from a deletion.", "At first the code was untouched. About an hour earlier the repository had moved from its creator's personal account to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, created at 22:08 UTC. Old links redirected, and issues were still being updated after the server went dark. Around the same time the maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues, cutting the list from nearly 4,900 to about 200.", "GitHub's public DMCA log shows no notice against the project. The disappearance follows other pressure on GTA VI communities: earlier this month the GTA 6 Mapping Project's Discord vanished without explanation, and in August Take-Two sought subpoenas against Discord to identify the leaker, which Discord said it hadn't been served.", 'Update, 23:47 UTC: the GitHub repository has since been deleted, and its creator says he has quit. See our follow-up.']

events.note: ["A developer who goes by Marvis livestreamed GTA VI running on a PC on Monday, getting as far as the game's menus at roughly 15 frames per second. No public project has shown that much yet: Leonida, XCL and TuxBox all run the game's own code, but their screens are still black or blank.", "Late on Monday he published the code on GitHub as VIctory, a Rust layer that runs the game's own code natively on Windows. Its README goes further than the stream: boot screens, intro video, start screen and saves work at 30 fps, and loading reaches the open world, where the picture stays black and the graphics card fails within seconds.", "Viewers who went through the stream closely mostly concluded it is genuine. A staged fake would take a very elaborate setup, and few think that is what happened. The timing also fits: an outside contributor's unmerged change to XCL reports reaching the first menus on the same day.", "VIctory sits at our Main menu stage, 55%. Its results are still his own, from one PC with an AMD RX 6700 XT; we'll update the entry as others try the code, and take it down if the run turns out to be staged."]
events.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

events.title: Leonida gets GTA VI's executable running, but nothing is on screen yet
events.note: ["Hours after Cyberleek's executable appeared on Monday, Leonida's contributors began running it through the project's runtime and logging each attempt in a shared issue. On builds that stack about 25 unmerged pull requests, the retail executable now runs its own code for up to three minutes on Windows, Wine and Proton. It sets up the graphics device, gets through audio setup, builds tens of thousands of graphics pipelines and opens a window.", "That window stays blank. The current wall is a console-only call on the game's command allocators that the PC layer doesn't answer, so frames never finish. None of the boot fixes are in Leonida's main branch yet, and contributors call merging them the bottleneck.", 'Posts in Leonida\'s Discord server told the same story. Soon after the drop, one said the game won\'t be playable today, "but maybe tomorrow". Later, another said it "almost boots", with a black screen and audio that cuts off. We can\'t check that timeline, and the repo still lists input, saves and streaming as not started.', "Leonida isn't alone. XCL runs a retail game its notes identify by GTA VI's executable at 30 fps on a black screen, and TuxBox shows the same black window on Proton. All three now sit at our Exe runs stage, 25%. None has drawn a picture."]
events.analysis: 涉及速度变化；需要核对游戏内 FPS、硬件及统计口径。

events.title: Cyberleek's README frames the leak as a protest and asks for crypto
events.note: ["A text file said to be the README from Cyberleek's archive was shared on Reddit on Nov 23, shortly after the executable drop. We haven't seen the archive ourselves, so we can't confirm the note is genuine. Here is everything it says, in our words.", 'It casts the leaks as a fight against what it calls anti-consumer habits in games: subscriptions added to single-player titles, pricey special editions that only unlock content already in the files, and licences sold as if they were purchases. Its own summary: "The enemy is the tactic, not the game." It says players were never the target, which is why the ending and story were kept out of the leaks, and that every release since its first clip in August 2026 has cost nothing.', "Then it turns defiant. It claims months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing haven't stopped the uploads, and argues that money can't make any protection unbreakable and courts can't pull back what has already spread online.", "Next comes the money. The note says donations fund a project it won't describe until there's something to show, and that some money has already arrived and paid for the first steps. It says the skills behind the build would earn more in other, quieter work, while insisting that isn't a threat. Backers, it says, can only change how fast that project becomes its main focus, not where it goes. It promises future releases will be free whether or not anyone pays, but counts every donation and every trade of its token as a vote.",

events.title: Cyberleek says the missing GTA VI executable is out, hours before its own deadline
events.note: ['Cyberleek posted on Monday, Nov 23 at 15:36 CET (14:36 UTC) that the executable missing from its leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI is now out. That is about two and a half hours before the 18:00 CET deadline the leaker had set itself. The post calls the release free and says it hands the work over to the open-source recompilation and emulation projects.', "We haven't downloaded or checked the file, and we won't link to it. When we published, no outlet had confirmed it is genuine. The post also asks for crypto donations, and Cyberleek has tied earlier releases to a token, so treat the claims around it with care.", "Expect fakes. Leaked files are an easy way to spread malware, and fake GTA VI downloads were circulating before this drop. Don't run executables you got from strangers, and only use the original project repositories linked in the race on our homepage.", 'For the race, this is the starting gun: until now no project could even try to boot GTA VI. Nothing on the tracker changes until one shows it running, and the countdown on our homepage now counts up from the release.']

events.note: ["The X account of boykopovar, the developer of PS5-to-PC tool AnyPS5, is suspended. We saw the notice on the profile on Nov 22. It showed no evidence that either company was involved, and we found no reporting or statement that says so. We couldn't confirm an earlier suspension either.", "AnyPS5 itself is still online: new code reached its GitHub repository later that day. One project we track, americas-recomp, is a fork of it. The suspension doesn't change any scores or show progress on running GTA VI.", "Be careful with what travels alongside this story. The account making the claim promotes a token using the project's name and says the developer supports it. We haven't verified that, and saw no mention of a token in the project's README or on the developer's public Telegram channel. Don't treat the suspension as a reason to buy one."]

events.title: XCL takes the lead after running its first retail Xbox games on PC
events.note: ["XCL runs Xbox Series code natively and swaps in its own versions of the console's system libraries. On Nov 22 its README began reporting that Minecraft Preview is fully playable on a PC, with worlds, sound and a controller. Fortnite and XDefiant reach their title screens and menus, going as far as they can without their online services.", "Its commit history over the day matches that account: Fortnite's splash screen in the morning, Minecraft's main menu by early afternoon and a playable build by the evening. The results are self-reported, and nobody else has reproduced them yet.", "For GTA VI, XCL says all 26,698 GPU programs in the game's shader pack translate to HLSL and that sampled ones compile for PC. Running another retail game end to end is the strongest sign yet that a layer like this could carry GTA VI. XCL's score rises to about 22%, ahead of xbox-emulator.", "Elsewhere, americas-recomp now translates almost all of the game's shaders, and Leonida's loader runs a stand-in program end to end. Every project is still waiting on the same file."]

events.title: The missing GTA VI executable is due Monday at 18:00 CET, and votes cost money
events.note: ['Cyberleek\'s own countdown for the withheld executable ends on Monday, Nov 23 at 18:00 CET (17:00 UTC), and RockstarINTEL reports the same deadline. That is more precise than the "Monday" first announced, and it is the time the countdown on this page now uses.', "The leaker's site pairs the timer with a poll on what happens next, and votes are cast by paying in cryptocurrency. RockstarINTEL also reports that the token goal for an early release has dropped to $6 million, after $30 million in October and $15 million earlier this week. Reports put the token at about $1.4 million.", "None of this is verified. No outlet has confirmed that the group holds a working executable, and Decrypt and others describe the countdown as a way to pump the token. The group ended a similar campaign in October when its goal wasn't met.", 'If a file does appear, expect fakes first. Security researchers have already found fake "GTA VI installers" carrying the Vidar info-stealer and hundreds of domains pushing fake launchers. This tracker will report a release only once outlets confirm it, and will never link to it.']

events.title: Re-uploads of the leading GTA VI projects are already circulating
events.note: ['Our scout ran for the first time on Saturday night. Among a dozen new repositories it found three that were not new projects at all: they were re-uploads of Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port, published under unrelated accounts.', "Two kept the original name. The third had been renamed to something that sounds like GTA, carried a one-line description, and had a README that was 97% identical to Leonida's.", "A re-upload isn't necessarily malicious. Plenty of people mirror code they find interesting. But a copied repo is the easiest place to slip a modified build script or a fake executable into something that looks trustworthy, and Leonida is built by double-clicking a batch file.", "From today, the scout compares every new repository's README against the projects we track and flags close copies instead of listing them. Unreviewed repositories are no longer linked from this site. If you're following a project, use only the original repository linked in the race."]

events.title: Cyberleek's Xbox build is out, except the file that runs it
events.note: ["Cyberleek, the group behind this year's GTA VI footage leaks, says it has released a roughly 209 GB Xbox Series build of the game, labelled version 1.0.2.1, by torrent. The game's main executable is not included.", "According to the group's statement, the executable will be released on Monday, Nov 23, with no conditions attached. It says the file will come out immediately if its CYBERLEEK token reaches a $15 million market cap first.", 'No outlet or security researcher has independently verified that the files are a genuine GTA VI build, and Rockstar and Take-Two have not commented. Projects on this tracker say they are working with a package whose contents match what they expect, including 26,503 shaders, but none can boot it without the executable.', 'Cyberleek also predicted that PC players would be emulating the build within a week. As Gamereactor points out, no working Xbox Series X|S emulator exists yet. That gap is exactly what the projects on this page are trying to close.']

events.title: Every “GTA VI for PC” download is fake, and some empty your accounts
events.note: ["There is no PC version of GTA VI. Rockstar hasn't announced one, and no community port can run the game yet. That hasn't stopped a wave of fake installers.", 'Kaspersky has logged more than 27,000 detections of GTA VI-themed malware and unwanted software since June. ESET found a file named gta6_installer.exe carrying the Vidar infostealer. Cynet analysed a fake download that installs a stealer which takes saved passwords, browser cookies, Steam and Roblox logins and crypto wallet data.', 'NordVPN researchers also found a dark-web bundle selling for about $200 in crypto. It lets low-skill scammers run their own fake GTA VI download campaigns.', "The warning signs are consistent. Instructions ask you to run the file as administrator, click past security warnings or add an antivirus exclusion, and some offers ask for payment in crypto or gift cards. With Cyberleek's missing executable due Monday, expect a flood of files claiming to be it. If you've already run one, treat the PC as compromised and change your passwords from a different device."]

events.title: Take-Two hits GTA V ports on GitHub, saying “bring your own files” is no defence
events.note: ['On Nov 18, the day before GTA VI launched, Take-Two sent GitHub four DMCA takedown notices aimed at unofficial GTA V ports. The targets included an iOS and macOS port, a multi-platform runtime, an Android port, and repositories linked to a browser-based version.', "Reports differ on the scale. One counted 349 disabled forks of a single port, while another headline put the total above 600 projects. GitHub didn't publish a final count.", "The argument matters more than the numbers. Three of the four projects shipped no game files and told users to supply their own copy. Take-Two's notices argue that this setup doesn't excuse helping people reproduce the game without permission.", 'Every GTA VI project on this tracker uses the same “use your own copy” disclaimer. Developers can contest a takedown with a counter-notice, which obliges GitHub to restore the code unless Take-Two sues, as it did over the re3 and reVC projects in 2021.']

events.title: The 2022 GTA VI hacker pleads guilty and will be sentenced on Monday
events.note: ['Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the September 2022 leak of early GTA VI development footage, pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court in London on Nov 16. He admitted hacking Rockstar Games and putting roughly 90 clips online.', 'The charges also cover intrusions at other companies. He is due to be sentenced at the same court on Monday, Nov 23, the same day Cyberleek says it will release the missing executable for its leaked Xbox build.', "The two leaks are separate. The 2022 breach exposed unfinished footage from inside Rockstar. Cyberleek's 2026 release claims to be a finished console build of the shipped game."]

after.title: ZETTROX's GTA VI build looks uncrashable so far
after.note: ['ZETTROX\'s build of GTA VI hasn\'t crashed yet. It has played from Lucia\'s prologue into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing", where it showed the first kill with a gun in GTA VI on PC, and it hasn\'t gone down once along the way. Its README reports more than an hour and a half in one session without a crash.', 'That\'s rare this early. Running a game built for other hardware usually means crashing, and often. ZETTROX\'s is the only build on our board rated better than "Crashes sometimes": on Wednesday its stability went from 0.5 to 0.8 ("Rarely crashes"), which puts it first at 64.2%.', "It's also slowly getting toward free roam, the point where the story lets go and the open world is yours. That takes patience: the build runs at 1 to 3 frames per second, and the picture is still poor, with anything in shadow drawn black and bright scenes overexposed.", "What keeps it running isn't clear yet. Like Uilian's VItoriaBr, it's based on VIctory and hyphennn's victory-fork, with ZETTROX's own work for NVIDIA cards, tested on an RTX 3050. Unlike most builds this far along, its code is public, as Zettrox/ztrx, so anyone can compare it with victory-fork and find what's different."]
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: GTA VI builds clear Lucia's prologue and reach Jason's first mission
after.note: ['Several private PC builds of GTA VI can now play through Lucia\'s prologue and carry on into Jason\'s first mission, "Gone Fishing". Until now, the furthest builds we track had only reached the prologue itself, so this is the deepest into the story anyone has reported.', "It's rough. Most builds still render the world badly, and vehicles don't work most of the time: in Gone Fishing the boat often can't be steered. On some builds, the map in the pause menu opens.", "We can't say yet whose builds these are. The people getting this far are working in private, and most of them appear to build on hyphennn's victory-fork, the public fork of VIctory behind the top of our board. Their own changes aren't public, so nobody else can test them.", '"Prologue cleared" is the first step of our story track, but no score changes until we know which builds did it. If yours is one of them, open an issue on our GitHub with a link to a recording or a stream.']
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: Take-Two's first GTA VI port takedown disables Leonida and 3,007 forks
after.note: ['Take-Two has filed its first DMCA notice against a GTA VI port. The notice, published in GitHub\'s public DMCA log on Tuesday, names ItsNotRexed\'s Leonida repository. Because the fork network was larger than 100 repositories and Take-Two said the forks infringe just as the original does, GitHub processed it against the whole network: 3,007 repositories. Contributor forks that survived Leonida\'s shutdown on Monday now show GitHub\'s "unavailable" page.', 'The publisher calls Leonida a derivative work of GTA VI and says it breaches the reverse-engineering ban in Rockstar\'s terms of service. It also argues that the project\'s "bring your own files" line is misleading: given the timing, it says, the files users must supply can only be the leaked Xbox build.', "The notice names only Leonida. Projects that aren't GitHub forks of it, such as VIctory and XCL, and Leonida copies uploaded as new repositories, are still online for now. But the same argument could apply to any of them.", 'Leonida stays on our board as nuked, for the record.']
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: PortWatch's new scale: Playable is halfway, finishing the game is 100%
after.note: ['We\'ve changed how PortWatch scores projects. The old bar climbed from groundwork to "In-game", then to 30 FPS and "Stable". Many of you pointed out that this mixed up two different things: getting the game to run at all, and having it play well. Walking around a dark world at 5 frames per second isn\'t three-quarters of the way to playing GTA VI on PC.', 'Getting in is now a ladder to 50%. Groundwork fills the first 10%. Then come Exe runs (10%), First frame (20%), Main menu (30%), In the world (40%), when story mode loads the world and draws it, however broken, and Playable (50%), when you control a character in it.', 'Past Playable, four tracks fill the other half side by side: story progress (35 points), from stuck in the opening to 100% completion; rendering (25), from black or broken to matching the console; performance (20), the average frame rate divided by 30; and stability (20). 100% now means the whole game can be finished, looking like the console, at 30 fps or better, without crashing.', "Every project has been re-scored, and the numbers are lower. The furthest builds are now just past halfway: hyphennn's private build at 59.4%, omonkey's at 57.9%, victory-gta6 at 57.3% and CGBJ's at 54.5%. VIctory is at 40%, in the world but not yet playable, and XCL at 35%. Nobody went backwards: the same results now count for less of the whole game.", 'The history chart has been converted to the new scale too. after.title: GTA VI's shaders start loading on omonkey's build, streamed live on Rumble
after.note: ["A developer called omonkey has GTA VI running on PC with its shaders starting to load properly. It runs at about 5 frames per second and is stuck in the opening scene, Lucia's prison, but a player can move around in it, slowly.", 'That puts omonkey ahead of every project we track. CGBJ, which we added earlier on Tuesday, also has a player moving, but on a black screen, and a video of it shows the opening in flat colours without lighting.', "omonkey streams all of his development work on Rumble, but not on a channel of his own. The streams go out on Swaggely, a channel with about 1,800 followers that belongs to a separate person. It isn't clear why the two work this way.", "We've added omonkey to the tracker at 76%, at our In-game stage, which puts him first. Because the work has been streamed live the whole time, we're confident it's real. We haven't found any public code from him, though, so nobody can test it outside the streams yet.", "Update, 20:10 UTC: omonkey's build is based on victory-gta6, fxceless's public fork of VIctory, which we've now added to the race at 74%. Our race now ranks only projects with public code, so omonkey's private build is listed below it without a rank. At 76% it still leads our overall progress number, and it shows on victory-gta6's card as a build on that code."]

after.title: Exclusive: CGBJ gets GTA VI in game, walking and talking in an unlit world
after.note: ['A group called CGBJ has got GTA VI into its game world on PC, and a player can move in it. With a controller they walk around, talk to NPCs and open the in-game menu. PortWatch has verified that it gets in game. No public project has shown a player moving yet.', "It is far from playable, and it runs very slowly. In the run where a player walked around, the screen was black. A 77-second video posted on X on Tuesday shows more: GTA VI's opening scenes in flat colours with no lighting, from a car's interior to a street of waving NPCs, a guard and a prison yard.", "CGBJ's code is private. It builds on VIctory, the open-source layer whose author first showed GTA VI's menus on a livestream on Monday, and also takes some of XCL's work. Both are public on GitHub; CGBJ's changes aren't, so nobody outside the group can test them.", "We've added CGBJ to the tracker at 72%, at our In-game stage, which puts it first. That rests on our own check: the video doesn't name the project, and nobody outside the group can reproduce the result yet.", "Update, 20:10 UTC: our race now ranks only projects with public code, so CGBJ's private build is listed below it without a rank, still at 72%. It counts toward our overall progress number, which omonkey's private build now leads at 76%, and it shows on the cards of VIctory and XCL as a build on their code."]

after.title: Exclusive: XCL reports 30 fps in GTA VI but won't say if it's past the menus
after.note: ["XCL says GTA VI now runs at 30 frames per second in game, but won't say where. Asked whether that means the menus it had already reached or actual gameplay, the team refused to answer, saying it feared being nuked. Privately, it hinted to one of our community members that things are working really well.", 'Its public notes haven\'t caught up. XCL\'s README still calls the game "a newer retail game" that reaches its menus at a steady 30 fps, with gameplay not reached yet. Early on Tuesday the project merged a change that shows the live frame rate in the game window\'s title.', "The caution runs through the scene. XCL's Discord server is tightly locked down with its chats closed, and members are scared of being nuked after Leonida lost its server, its repository and its creator within an hour on Monday night. The GTA 6 Modding Discord server has now been nuked too.", 'Update, 01:50 UTC: testers on XCL\'s GitHub now report GTA VI getting past its menus into the world on the public code. The game\'s own state reads "Game Running", but the screen stays on a loading spinner and a GPU watchdog ends each run within minutes. One report claims gameplay at 28 to 30 fps, without a screenshot. XCL moves to 62.5%, halfway to In-game.']

after.title: TuxBox draws GTA VI's first screen as VIctory edges into the world
after.note: ["Leonida's exit hasn't slowed the other GTA VI ports. TuxBox, a compatibility layer tested mostly on Linux through Proton, published a run record showing the game's player-selection prompt at 4K on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. It hasn't sent the game any input yet, so we count it as a first frame, not a menu. That takes TuxBox from 25% to 40%.", "VIctory, level with XCL at the main menu, now says its runs reach the world. The first mission's title card renders, but the scene behind it stays dark at roughly one frame every one to two seconds, and the project warns that real GPUs can hang. That isn't playable, so VIctory stays at 55%.", 'PercyScarlett reports GTA VI running to a frame loop of black frames before the GPU hangs, and a new project, GTA6-BootTest, gets its exe through the same stage with stand-in DLLs. Both now sit at "Exe runs". As always, these are the projects\' own reports; none has been reproduced independently.']
