after.title: Leonida is nuked: GitHub repo deleted, Discord gone, creator quits
after.note: ['Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port with more than 33,000 GitHub stars, went offline in under an hour on Monday night. Its Discord server stopped resolving at about 23:07 UTC. By 23:47 its GitHub repository was gone. Around the same time its creator, NotRexed, posted "I quit guys" on X, writing that he kept running into problems he couldn\'t control and was stepping away, and thanking the Discord community.', 'The repository now answers "not found", not the "unavailable" page GitHub shows after a DMCA takedown, and GitHub\'s public DMCA log has no notice against it. That points to its owners pulling it rather than Take-Two, though only they can say. Earlier that evening it had moved to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, whose maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues.', "The code isn't lost. Contributors' forks are still on GitHub, among them the one carrying the combined boot fixes, and a mirror on NotRexed's own Git server holds the code as of 23:30 UTC, though it can no longer sync.", "We've marked Leonida as nuked on the tracker. It stays on the board for the record but no longer counts in the rankings.", "Update, Nov 24: Take-Two has since filed a DMCA notice against Leonida, published in GitHub's log on Nov 24, and GitHub disabled the repository's whole network of 3,007 forks, including the contributor fork linked below. Copies uploaded as separate repositories are not part of that network."]
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: Leonida's Discord server disappears as the project moves to a new GitHub account
after.note: ["Leonida's Discord server went offline late on Monday. At 23:06 UTC its invite still led to a server of about 179,000 members, 74,000 of them online. Within a minute Discord answered that both the invite and the server were unknown. Members say Discord banned it. Neither Discord nor the Leonida team has said why, and from outside we can't tell a ban from a deletion.", "At first the code was untouched. About an hour earlier the repository had moved from its creator's personal account to a new organization, ProjectLeonida, created at 22:08 UTC. Old links redirected, and issues were still being updated after the server went dark. Around the same time the maintainers closed thousands of open pull requests and issues, cutting the list from nearly 4,900 to about 200.", "GitHub's public DMCA log shows no notice against the project. The disappearance follows other pressure on GTA VI communities: earlier this month the GTA 6 Mapping Project's Discord vanished without explanation, and in August Take-Two sought subpoenas against Discord to identify the leaker, which Discord said it hadn't been served.", 'Update, 23:47 UTC: the GitHub repository has since been deleted, and its creator says he has quit. See our follow-up.']
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: Exclusive: Marvis livestreams GTA VI reaching its menus at about 15 fps
after.note: ["A developer who goes by Marvis livestreamed GTA VI running on a PC on Monday, getting as far as the game's menus at roughly 15 frames per second. No public project has shown that much yet: Leonida, XCL and TuxBox all run the game's own code, but their screens are still black or blank.", "Late on Monday he published the code on GitHub as VIctory, a Rust layer that runs the game's own code natively on Windows. Its README goes further than the stream: boot screens, intro video, start screen and saves work at 30 fps, and loading reaches the open world, where the picture stays black and the graphics card fails within seconds.", "Viewers who went through the stream closely mostly concluded it is genuine. A staged fake would take a very elaborate setup, and few think that is what happened. The timing also fits: an outside contributor's unmerged change to XCL reports reaching the first menus on the same day.", "VIctory sits at our Main menu stage, 55%. Its results are still his own, from one PC with an AMD RX 6700 XT; we'll update the entry as others try the code, and take it down if the run turns out to be staged."]

after.title: Leonida gets GTA VI's executable running, but nothing is on screen yet
after.note: ["Hours after Cyberleek's executable appeared on Monday, Leonida's contributors began running it through the project's runtime and logging each attempt in a shared issue. On builds that stack about 25 unmerged pull requests, the retail executable now runs its own code for up to three minutes on Windows, Wine and Proton. It sets up the graphics device, gets through audio setup, builds tens of thousands of graphics pipelines and opens a window.", "That window stays blank. The current wall is a console-only call on the game's command allocators that the PC layer doesn't answer, so frames never finish. None of the boot fixes are in Leonida's main branch yet, and contributors call merging them the bottleneck.", 'Posts in Leonida\'s Discord server told the same story. Soon after the drop, one said the game won\'t be playable today, "but maybe tomorrow". Later, another said it "almost boots", with a black screen and audio that cuts off. We can\'t check that timeline, and the repo still lists input, saves and streaming as not started.', "Leonida isn't alone. XCL runs a retail game its notes identify by GTA VI's executable at 30 fps on a black screen, and TuxBox shows the same black window on Proton. All three now sit at our Exe runs stage, 25%. None has drawn a picture."]
after.analysis: 涉及速度变化；需要核对游戏内 FPS、硬件及统计口径。

after.title: Cyberleek's README frames the leak as a protest and asks for crypto
after.note: ["A text file said to be the README from Cyberleek's archive was shared on Reddit on Nov 23, shortly after the executable drop. We haven't seen the archive ourselves, so we can't confirm the note is genuine. Here is everything it says, in our words.", 'It casts the leaks as a fight against what it calls anti-consumer habits in games: subscriptions added to single-player titles, pricey special editions that only unlock content already in the files, and licences sold as if they were purchases. Its own summary: "The enemy is the tactic, not the game." It says players were never the target, which is why the ending and story were kept out of the leaks, and that every release since its first clip in August 2026 has cost nothing.', "Then it turns defiant. It claims months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing haven't stopped the uploads, and argues that money can't make any protection unbreakable and courts can't pull back what has already spread online.", "Next comes the money. The note says donations fund a project it won't describe until there's something to show, and that some money has already arrived and paid for the first steps. It says the skills behind the build would earn more in other, quieter work, while insisting that isn't a threat. Backers, it says, can only change how fast that project becomes its main focus, not where it goes. It promises future releases will be free whether or not anyone pays, but counts every donation and every trade of its token as a vote.",
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: Cyberleek says the missing GTA VI executable is out, hours before its own deadline
after.note: ['Cyberleek posted on Monday, Nov 23 at 15:36 CET (14:36 UTC) that the executable missing from its leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI is now out. That is about two and a half hours before the 18:00 CET deadline the leaker had set itself. The post calls the release free and says it hands the work over to the open-source recompilation and emulation projects.', "We haven't downloaded or checked the file, and we won't link to it. When we published, no outlet had confirmed it is genuine. The post also asks for crypto donations, and Cyberleek has tied earlier releases to a token, so treat the claims around it with care.", "Expect fakes. Leaked files are an easy way to spread malware, and fake GTA VI downloads were circulating before this drop. Don't run executables you got from strangers, and only use the original project repositories linked in the race on our homepage.", 'For the race, this is the starting gun: until now no project could even try to boot GTA VI. Nothing on the tracker changes until one shows it running, and the countdown on our homepage now counts up from the release.']
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: AnyPS5 developer suspended on X, with no evidence Sony or Rockstar was behind it
after.note: ["The X account of boykopovar, the developer of PS5-to-PC tool AnyPS5, is suspended. We saw the notice on the profile on Nov 22. It points to X's rules in general and doesn't say which one was broken or whether anyone complained.", "An account describing itself as AnyPS5's community account called it a repeat suspension and suggested Sony and Rockstar fear the project. It showed no evidence that either company was involved, and we found no reporting or statement that says so. We couldn't confirm an earlier suspension either.", "AnyPS5 itself is still online: new code reached its GitHub repository later that day. One project we track, americas-recomp, is a fork of it. The suspension doesn't change any scores or show progress on running GTA VI.", "Be careful with what travels alongside this story. The account making the claim promotes a token using the project's name and says the developer supports it. We haven't verified that, and saw no mention of a token in the project's README or on the developer's public Telegram channel. Don't treat the suspension as a reason to buy one."]

after.title: XCL takes the lead after running its first retail Xbox games on PC
after.note: ["XCL runs Xbox Series code natively and swaps in its own versions of the console's system libraries. On Nov 22 its README began reporting that Minecraft Preview is fully playable on a PC, with worlds, sound and a controller. Fortnite and XDefiant reach their title screens and menus, going as far as they can without their online services.", "Its commit history over the day matches that account: Fortnite's splash screen in the morning, Minecraft's main menu by early afternoon and a playable build by the evening. The results are self-reported, and nobody else has reproduced them yet.", "For GTA VI, XCL says all 26,698 GPU programs in the game's shader pack translate to HLSL and that sampled ones compile for PC. Running another retail game end to end is the strongest sign yet that a layer like this could carry GTA VI. XCL's score rises to about 22%, ahead of xbox-emulator.", "Elsewhere, americas-recomp now translates almost all of the game's shaders, and Leonida's loader runs a stand-in program end to end. Every project is still waiting on the same file."]

after.title: The missing GTA VI executable is due Monday at 18:00 CET, and votes cost money
after.note: ['Cyberleek\'s own countdown for the withheld executable ends on Monday, Nov 23 at 18:00 CET (17:00 UTC), and RockstarINTEL reports the same deadline. That is more precise than the "Monday" first announced, and it is the time the countdown on this page now uses.', "The leaker's site pairs the timer with a poll on what happens next, and votes are cast by paying in cryptocurrency. RockstarINTEL also reports that the token goal for an early release has dropped to $6 million, after $30 million in October and $15 million earlier this week. Reports put the token at about $1.4 million.", "None of this is verified. No outlet has confirmed that the group holds a working executable, and Decrypt and others describe the countdown as a way to pump the token. The group ended a similar campaign in October when its goal wasn't met.", 'If a file does appear, expect fakes first. Security researchers have already found fake "GTA VI installers" carrying the Vidar info-stealer and hundreds of domains pushing fake launchers. This tracker will report a release only once outlets confirm it, and will never link to it.']

after.title: Re-uploads of the leading GTA VI projects are already circulating
after.note: ['Our scout ran for the first time on Saturday night. Among a dozen new repositories it found three that were not new projects at all: they were re-uploads of Leonida, the most-starred GTA VI port, published under unrelated accounts.', "Two kept the original name. The third had been renamed to something that sounds like GTA, carried a one-line description, and had a README that was 97% identical to Leonida's.", "A re-upload isn't necessarily malicious. Plenty of people mirror code they find interesting. But a copied repo is the easiest place to slip a modified build script or a fake executable into something that looks trustworthy, and Leonida is built by double-clicking a batch file.", "From today, the scout compares every new repository's README against the projects we track and flags close copies instead of listing them. Unreviewed repositories are no longer linked from this site. If you're following a project, use only the original repository linked in the race."]
after.analysis: 发现公开更新；尚未据此提高技术阶段。

after.title: Every “GTA VI for PC” download is fake, and some empty your accounts
after.note: ["There is no PC version of GTA VI. Rockstar hasn't announced one, and no community port can run the game yet. That hasn't stopped a wave of fake installers.", 'Kaspersky has logged more than 27,000 detections of GTA VI-themed malware and unwanted software since June. ESET found a file named gta6_installer.exe carrying the Vidar infostealer. Cynet analysed a fake download that installs a stealer which takes saved passwords, browser cookies, Steam and Roblox logins and crypto wallet data.', 'NordVPN researchers also found a dark-web bundle selling for about $200 in crypto. It lets low-skill scammers run their own fake GTA VI download campaigns.', "The warning signs are consistent. Instructions ask you to run the file as administrator, click past security warnings or add an antivirus exclusion, and some offers ask for payment in crypto or gift cards. With Cyberleek's missing executable due Monday, expect a flood of files claiming to be it. If you've already run one, treat the PC as compromised and change your passwords from a different device."]

after.title: Take-Two hits GTA V ports on GitHub, saying “bring your own files” is no defence
after.note: ['On Nov 18, the day before GTA VI launched, Take-Two sent GitHub four DMCA takedown notices aimed at unofficial GTA V ports. The targets included an iOS and macOS port, a multi-platform runtime, an Android port, and repositories linked to a browser-based version.', "Reports differ on the scale. One counted 349 disabled forks of a single port, while another headline put the total above 600 projects. GitHub didn't publish a final count.", "The argument matters more than the numbers. Three of the four projects shipped no game files and told users to supply their own copy. Take-Two's notices argue that this setup doesn't excuse helping people reproduce the game without permission.", 'Every GTA VI project on this tracker uses the same “use your own copy” disclaimer. Developers can contest a takedown with a counter-notice, which obliges GitHub to restore the code unless Take-Two sues, as it did over the re3 and reVC projects in 2021.']

after.title: The 2022 GTA VI hacker pleads guilty and will be sentenced on Monday

The 2022 breach exposed unfinished footage from inside Rockstar. Cyberleek's 2026 release claims to be a finished console build of the shipped game."]

after.title: XSXEmu starts the game's code on a Mac without Wine; correction on TuxBox's stage
after.note: XSXEmu starts the game's code on a Mac without Wine; correction on TuxBox's stage  XSXEmu's README now says the game's own code runs under Rosetta on Apple Silicon, starts its worker threads and opens its archives. after.title: We've seen Belobug's AMD build, and it's way ahead
after.note: ["We've seen Belobug's build of GTA VI running, and the PortWatch team thinks it's way ahead of every other build we track. The open world renders lit, with textures, people, vehicles, vegetation, water and sky, and it looks close to the retail game, just very slowly. It plays through missions, and it rarely crashes.", 'It went straight to #1 on our board at 77.4%, more than 13 points clear of ZETTROX\'s 64.2%, which led until this morning. Its rendering is rated 0.85 on our scale, the highest we\'ve given any build, and its story progress 0.5 ("First act"). The next best picture, suri\'s private build, is at 0.8; ZETTROX\'s, which draws anything in shadow black, is at 0.3.', "It's built for AMD Radeon, while ZETTROX's, the previous leader, is tuned for NVIDIA. Belobug runs it on a Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB of RAM and Windows 11. It's a fork of Marvis's VIctory, following its main branch plus upstream pull requests, and its README says no code from hyphennn's victory-fork is in it. Belobug's own fixes include a stand-in for the game's ray-traced indirect light, which left leaves magenta and indoor scenes in coloured blocks, a fix for lines along every triangle on car paint, glass and skin, and a change that cut the GPU time of one heavy scene from 225 to about 80 milliseconds a frame.", 'It isn\'t fast. after.title: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment
after.note: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment  VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README (14:00 UTC) says its stand-in for ray-traced light is now weaker in creases and under objects, and that the game's own sun and lamp shadows work. It still reports 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, says about 380 draws a frame are dropped, and says the frame is bound by the processor's work. VIctory-macOS reports its current code staying in the world for over 20 minutes without freezing on an M3 Max, at 0.1 to 0.2 frames a second. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project. VIniVIdiVIci, a fork of victory-fork checked on an RTX 4060 Ti, joins the watch list at a reader's request. Its README says it has not yet published results of its own in play. The estimate is unchanged at the evening of Thu 26 Nov.     14:01  25 Nov

after.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
after.note: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first  Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count. Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3. The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. A project that reports no run length counts as having none, which is why VItoriaBr and ScarlettPort sit lower than before. The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. Stages below 6 have no lanes and are still ordered by this page's reading.      See 118 earlier updates    13:04  25 Nov

after.title: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8
after.note: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8  At 12:20 UTC this page reported victory-fork's first room at 6.0 frames a second by default and 8.9 with a newer draw path. At 12:43 UTC the project withdrew both figures: its README says the two runs stood in different scenes and could not be compared. Its corrected figures come from one run each on an RTX 4070. At the same load a frame takes 145 ms with the newer path off and 124 ms with it on and memory copies made in place, about 6.9 and 8.1 frames a second. On screen it reports 7 to 8 in the first rooms and 10 to 12 in lighter views. The same notes describe a first play session past the first rooms. It reached the open world and lost the graphics device there in about 13 minutes, with the 12 GB card out of room for new textures, and the cause is not known. The estimate does not move: the gain is smaller than first stated, ordinary play is still under 10 frames a second, and nothing was withdrawn as unstable. Also in this check, ScarlettPort reports its frozen overlay fixed, still at about 4 frames a second, and VIctory-macOS reports its loading freezes on Macs fixed.     12:38  25 Nov

after.title: Rows at stage 6 now show three lanes: picture, speed and stability
after.note: Rows at stage 6 now show three lanes: picture, speed and stability  Thirteen projects sit at stage 6, so each of their rows now carries three more meters. Speed is the best average the project reports in play, stability is the longest session it reports without a crash, and picture follows written steps. The key under the standings title lists them, and blue marks the steps that meet the playable bar. On speed, the front of the field is at step 3 of 6, from 5 to 9 frames a second: victory-fork at 8.9, klbf-lab at 8.4 and AnyXboxX at 6.9. victory-perf's unconfirmed 9 to 14 reads as step 4. Playable asks for step 5, 20 frames a second. On stability, klbf-lab and ztrx report sessions of more than an hour, and victory-fork's code and AnyXboxX pass the 30 minutes the bar asks for. On picture, VIctory-Belobug-AMD and one private build read as lit and whole, and most of the others still have black or dark shadows. The lanes were suggested by a reader in issue 8 on this page's repository.     12:20  25 Nov

after.title: Estimate held at its mid-morning review
after.note: Estimate held at its mid-morning review  The mid-morning review leaves the estimate at early on Fri 27 Nov. This was the check for moving it a quarter of a day later if speed had not moved. It has started to: victory-fork merged its first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC, and its notes name the cost that remains and a change that more than halves it but is not yet stable. It does not move earlier either. Nothing measured in a long run has beaten about 7.6 frames a second since 22:15 UTC on 24 November. victory-perf's 9 to 14 in interiors is still one unconfirmed report, the only other reduced-resolution measurement is 6.1 to 6.4 on an RTX 3090 Ti, and XCL has reported neither control nor a longer run. What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: a second report of 10 or more in play, a confirmation of victory-perf's figures by someone else, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork. Later by a quarter of a day: those figures withdrawn or contradicted, or none of the three by the review at about 13:30 UTC. News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. Today's coverage, heise's included, reports the Leonida takedown from the notice GitHub published. No notice names another project, and no outlet has covered or tested victory-perf.     08:38  25 Nov

after.note: XCL corrects its figure: about 5 frames a second in the world, not 14  XCL's README, changed at 06:23 UTC, now gives about 5 frames a second in the 3D world on an RTX 5090. Its commit note says the 14 it published at 04:53 UTC was the average of a whole 5-minute run with menus and loading included, and that the world ran at 5 to 6. It has lowered its own progress estimate from about 65 to about 60 percent. This page reported the 14 at 05:01 UTC as a whole-run average and did not count it as a frame rate in play. after.note: Take-Two is reported to be sending takedown notices over footage of unofficial builds  VGTimes and Twisted Voxel report, citing a post on X by the reporter Ben, that Take-Two is sending takedown notices over social media posts that show footage of unofficial PC builds. By VGTimes' account, one notice says the port is being developed from leaked copies of Rockstar's files and that the footage contains Rockstar's characters, environments and other material. Neither report names a platform, a number of notices or a project, and neither carries a statement from Take-Two. It is the first reported action since the notice against Leonida. No new notice has appeared in GitHub's public list. Neither company has commented since the build leaked. Before launch, Take-Two's chief executive said piracy would be met with legal and technical measures, and called unofficial PC ports made with AI a creative concern more than a financial one. It gives 4,307 frames in a 300-second run, which is 14 frames a second on average, and about 5 in the heaviest scene. The README does not split that run between the menus, which run at 30 frames a second, and the world, so 14 is not a frame rate in play. It calls the game not playable: the picture of the world is incomplete, with its minimap and other mesh pipelines refused, and it does not keep running there for long. It does not say whether the player has control. XCL is a separate code base from VIctory and its forks, so this is a second route into the game's world. after.title: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game
after.note: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game  An open pull request on victory-fork changes how the layer tracks the memory the game writes, and reports a drop from 390 ms to 9.8 ms a frame on an idle RTX 4090. That figure comes from a test program its author wrote, not from the game: the author says no game files were on the test PC. Its effect on the game has not been measured. Measured in the game: an open pull request on VIctory cuts the graphics time of a world frame on an RX 9070 XT under Proton from 600 to 720 ms down to 150 to 310 ms, and one on the fork takes an RTX 3070 laptop card in Series S mode from 353 ms to 305 ms a frame. None of these is merged, and none is a new top speed: the best measured figure in play is still about 7.6 frames a second. after.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
after.note: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first  Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count. Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3. The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. Its notes put the old cost at 0.45 to 0.7 seconds of a 1.5 to 1.7 second frame in the opening cutscene. The README's figure of 1 to 2 seconds a frame is not yet updated. Correction: palmetto's commit history, public again since about 01:45 UTC , says the repository descends from the project network that received Take-Two's notice, and that references to the game and to that project were removed in response. This page said at 22:22 UTC that its files did not show that origin. five-star-recomp reports most of the opening cutscene's 3D passes now running. Its 3D world is still not visible, and long runs end in a GPU hang. Open pull requests on victory-fork and VIctory report fixes that let the game's ray-tracing structure builder run on NVIDIA cards and that restore material colours that came out black. Neither is merged.     01:28  25 Nov

after.title: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes
after.note: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes  ztrx, a build of victory-fork's code published at 01:11 UTC on 25 November , reports in its README the opening mission playable from start to finish on an RTX 3050 with 8 GB, in one session of more than 1 hour 30 minutes without a crash. It runs at 1 to 3 frames a second, and anything in shadow is black. It is the first public code to make that claim and the longest session reported by anyone. PortWatch, which first listed it as a private build, says it verified the build going on into the next mission. A second public build of the same code, VItoriaBr, joins the standings. Its README reports the opening scenes at about 3 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti and says the world is not yet playable, while PortWatch reports its live stream reaching the second mission at up to 4 frames a second. victory-fork's main branch now runs at about 4.3 frames a second on an RTX 4070 by default, up from about 2.5, and lights its first room for the first time. The estimate moves in by a quarter of a day, to about 2 days: stability now has two long reports, and speed is the only gap left.     01:06  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: Estimate reviewed and left at about 2½ days
after.note: Estimate reviewed and left at about 2½ days  The estimate was reviewed at 01:05 UTC on 25 November and is unchanged: about 2½ days, around midday on Fri 27 Nov. PortWatch now says it has verified one private build playing through the opening mission into the next, at about 2 frames a second with poor rendering. That speaks to how well the game runs, not how fast, so it does not move the estimate. No takedown notice names a front-runner. Palmwave's repository has been unreachable for nearly three hours, for reasons that are not known.     00:46  25 Nov

after.note: A public VIctory fork reports the first gameplay scene with textures and sunlight  victory-gta6, a fork of VIctory first published at 18:02 UTC , says in its README that the game's first gameplay scene renders with characters, textures, sky and sunlit surfaces, and that the HUD, pause menu and controller input work. after.note: GitHub publishes a Take-Two takedown notice against Leonida and its forks  GitHub's public list of takedown notices now carries one from Take-Two, dated 24 November, against Leonida's repository. after.title: PortWatch says it has found no build above 10 frames a second in free roam, two forks report longer sessions and victory-windows joins the table
after.note: PortWatch says it has found no build above 10 frames a second in free roam, two forks report longer sessions and victory-windows joins the table  PortWatch's owner pinned a note at 18:57 UTC saying it has found no evidence of any build above 10 frames a second in free roam, and that claims of more should be doubted. The higher figures on this page, on Flamingo's and victory-perf's rows, are those projects' own from one machine each and stay marked unconfirmed. VIniVIdiVIci's README ( 18:46 UTC ) now gives 3 to 5 frames a second by scene, with 3.2 measured under player control, and a 15-minute session that ran to its time limit without a crash. A 30-minute session also reached its limit, but the project does not count it because its shutdown was not recorded cleanly. victory-unified reports a second session of about 49 minutes, this one on its current build, ended like the first by a graphics-device failure, and says it has changed settings to prevent it. New row at stage 6: victory-windows, a fork of VIctory whose README reports the controllable first room at 4.3 to 7.5 frames a second on an RTX 4090, with no run length stated and no commit since 09:15 UTC . The card filter now offers Intel, for the three lower-stage projects that list test reports from Intel cards.     18:36  25 Nov

after.title: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days
after.note: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days  victory-fork's README ( 17:28 UTC ) reports a 370-second play session at 4.5 frames a second on average, against 10.3 standing still. Half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle, because the game maps every streamed texture page itself, about 850 pages in a frame that streams. Two attempts to cut that cost were taken back out, one after faces came out black or red. Its speed lane now reads from its two play sessions, 4.5 on its own RTX 4070 and 7.6 on an RTX 4090 in a pull request, and it stays 3rd. The estimate moves back by three quarters of a day, to midday on Fri 27 Nov. The best averages from sessions of play are 7.6 to 8.6 against the 20 the bar asks for, and the figures of 10 or more came from the lightest scenes. This replaces the check published for 22:00 UTC , and the estimate's note gives the next marks. PortWatch reported at 17:26 UTC that ztrx's repository and the account that published it are both gone, with no takedown notice published. This page has had no answer from the repository since 16:57 UTC , and the reason is still not known. VIniVIdiVIci moves to stage 6: its README reports the player in control on an RTX 4060 Ti at about 2 to 5 frames a second, with a 13-minute session and a dark picture. ruff-lab, asked for in issue 16 on this page's repository, joins at stage 5 with the world drawn at 3.2 to 3.6 frames
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held
after.note: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held  ztrx's repository has not answered since 16:57 UTC , in three checks over 25 minutes while every other tracked repository answered, the last of them after GitHub closed its incident at 16:52 UTC . GitHub's published list holds no notice that names it and PortWatch still lists it, so the reason is not known: a repository made private, deleted or disabled looks the same from outside. Its row keeps its last reported status, without a link. Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 7 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, from 3 to 5: 5.4 to 6.7 standing still in a scene of 8,400 draws, less while driving. Its README puts the gain down to letting the game's submissions return before the card is done and to using game memory in place instead of copying it. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it rises to 4th. BRVIctory-ka1qux has turned the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the first public build on this page to do so. Its README says it costs 0.05 to 0.1 seconds a frame and has been checked on one open-world street only, in four runs of 5 to 11 minutes without a crash. The estimate was reviewed at 17:24 UTC and held at about a day. For it: three code bases now report about 10 frames a second in early scenes, more builds and machines report every hour, and VIctory's own README says you can get into the game. Against it: those figures are best cases, victory-fork's

after.title: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering
after.note: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering  victory-fork's README ( 19:21 UTC ) claims no frame-rate gain and says its headline figures stand. A frame capture now built into the layer puts the card's time for the game's own commands at 15 to 25 milliseconds a frame in the opening cutscene, far less than a whole frame, and the project says the time taken by the layer's own work does not add up yet. Keeping part of the game's memory copies on the graphics card cut the time spent in frames longer than 250 milliseconds from 21 and 26% to 4 and 6% in the opening cutscene, in two launches each way. The project calls it a result, not yet a default, and reports two other changes that measured no gain and were dropped. It also says a review of the open pull requests for frame rate found no single large gain, and that the change it had listed as the large step would be a modest one on its test PC. victory-perf's repository stopped answering over git between 18:56 and 19:28 UTC : missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. It is the third build of victory-fork's code to become unavailable today, after ztrx and the private build omonkey, and a news sweep at 19:27 UTC found no report about it. Two more forks join the watch list: VIctory-forkAMD and HybridGt.     19:05  25 Nov

after.title: VI-BR-PORT joins the table near the top, and ruff-lab logs 21.8 minutes without player control
after.note: VI-BR-PORT joins the table near the top, and ruff-lab logs 21.8 minutes without player control  VI-BR-PORT, a fork of victory-fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, joins at stage 6. Its README, in Portuguese, reports control, the HUD and the pause menu working at 4 to 7 frames a second at 1080p on an RTX 4060 Ti, sessions of an hour without losing the graphics device, and all 25,758 of the game's shaders translating on that card, with everything in shadow black. These are its own figures and estimates from one machine. The length of those sessions places it 4th, 2 steps short of the playable bar. ruff-lab's results log now holds a session of 21.8 minutes without a crash at 3.23 frames a second on average on an 8 GB Radeon RX 6600 XT with a hard disk. It says player movement does not work yet because of a controller input problem, so it stays at stage 5. vilocity's README says its rainbow glitter is gone and every shader now translates, still at 3 to 7 frames a second. five-star-recomp's status page says boots now stay 5 to 7 minutes in the world, with the lit picture still wrong. News check: other trackers repeat that ztrx's repository and account are gone, and none gives a reason. GitHub's list holds no new notice, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked.      See 131 earlier updates    17:50  25 Nov

after.title: victory-unified reports 58 minutes without a crash, and PortWatch says the private stream build runs on VIctory's code
after.note: victory-unified reports 58 minutes without a crash, and PortWatch says the private stream build runs on VIctory's code  victory-unified's README ( 20:38 UTC ) reports about 58 minutes in one session with no crash on an RTX 3070 with 8 GB, from the opening into a later mission outdoors, at 2 to 3 frames a second. It follows a fix for the graphics-device failure that ended its two earlier sessions at about 49 minutes. PortWatch added at 20:30 UTC , on its owner's word, that darkworldhm builds on a fork of VIctory, which one is not known. The build is still self-reported and its figures are still a reading of a live stream; its row here says so. VIniVIdiVIci reports four sessions of ten minutes that ran to their time limit without a crash with a texture change for 8 GB cards. There is no commit at victory-fork since 19:39 UTC or on VIctory's main branch since 16:51 UTC , and victory-perf's repository still does not answer.     20:19  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed
after.note: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed  PortWatch's entry for darkworldhm stood for a round and was raised at 19:59 UTC : its owner now reports free roam at 5 to 24 frames a second on the stream, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading. The build joins the table as a private row in 11th place with every figure marked as relayed. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, the code is not public, no session length is given, and nothing says whether the counter shows rendered frames. PortWatch's pinned notes since then ask the streamer to release the code. A news sweep at 20:16 UTC found no second source for that build. Coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, no notice names another project, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked. A small Manifold market, with four traders, gives about 1 in 5 that GitHub publishes a Take-Two notice naming VIctory by the end of the year. Vice-Tay's maintainer confirmed the move from victory-windows in a request on this page's repository and says the length of its test sessions is unknown. victory-perf's repository still does not answer. The estimate is unchanged. A reading of a stream is not the measured session of 10 minutes or more, averaging 12 or more in rendered frames, that the published mark asks for.     19:57  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: PortWatch now reports a private build at about 12 frames a second in free roam, ruff-lab reaches stage 6, and the estimate is held
after.note: PortWatch now reports a private build at about 12 frames a second in free roam, ruff-lab reaches stage 6, and the estimate is held  PortWatch replaced its pinned note at 19:42 UTC : its owner now reports a private build, darkworldhm, shown on a live stream in free roam at 5 to 18 frames a second, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading, reportedly on an RTX 50-series card. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, its code is not public, what it builds on is not known, and nothing says whether the figure counts rendered frames only. This page waits one round, or for a second source, before giving a private build a row. ruff-lab moves to stage 6: its README now reports the player in control with a DualShock 4 on a Radeon RX 6600 XT with 8 GB, 16 GB of memory and a hard disk, in a 39-minute session without a crash at 3.6 frames a second on average. victory-fork's README ( 19:39 UTC ) now heads its status with 8 to 10 frames a second in the first rooms and 5 to 8.5 through the opening cutscene, measured with changes that are off by default, and its evening code is in the tree with no speed gain shown. victory-windows is now published as Vice-Tay by the same maintainer, and victory-perf's repository still does not answer. Estimate reviewed this round and held at midday on Friday 27 November. The stream figure is one viewer's reading with no session length and no word on frame generation, so the published mark for moving earlier is not met. Against it, three builds of victory-fork's code

after.title: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering
after.note: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering  victory-fork's README ( 19:21 UTC ) claims no frame-rate gain and says its headline figures stand. A frame capture now built into the layer puts the card's time for the game's own commands at 15 to 25 milliseconds a frame in the opening cutscene, far less than a whole frame, and the project says the time taken by the layer's own work does not add up yet. Keeping part of the game's memory copies on the graphics card cut the time spent in frames longer than 250 milliseconds from 21 and 26% to 4 and 6% in the opening cutscene, in two launches each way. The project calls it a result, not yet a default, and reports two other changes that measured no gain and were dropped. It also says a review of the open pull requests for frame rate found no single large gain, and that the change it had listed as the large step would be a modest one on its test PC. victory-perf's repository stopped answering over git between 18:56 and 19:28 UTC : missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. It is the third build of victory-fork's code to become unavailable today, after ztrx and the private build omonkey, and a news sweep at 19:27 UTC found no report about it. Two more forks join the watch list: VIctory-forkAMD and HybridGt.      See 134 earlier updates    19:05  25 Nov

after.title: AnyXboxX reports about 12 frames a second on a new base and takes first place, and the estimate moves to early Friday
after.note: AnyXboxX reports about 12 frames a second on a new base and takes first place, and the estimate moves to early Friday  AnyXboxX's README ( 20:50 UTC ) says its maintainer measured a median of 12.5 frames a second in the world on an RTX 4070 SUPER at 4K output, about 15 over the last minute with peaks at 30 and no crash, after moving its code to a base it calls Neptune: a packaged edition of VIctory, shipped with its source, whose author it says has no public contact. Its previous base ran at about 5 there. The README does not say how long the session ran, and the figures are its own, from one machine. By the rule AnyXboxX is now first, 1 step short of the playable bar. Its speed lane reads the new base; its stability lane is still a contributor's relayed 45 minutes on the earlier base, and the row says so. Kelvaroq is second. Kelvaroq's README now cites its place on this page and carries a banner for the AI product it is built with. The tester behind its 36-minute session is not named, nobody else has confirmed the session, and PortWatch does not track Kelvaroq as a separate effort because it reads its results as VIctory's and victory-fork's code. A place here is computed from what a project reports about itself and is not a verification; the Positions note now says so. The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to early on Friday 27 November: three reports this evening put play at 10 frames a second or more, though none meets the published mark to the letter, and new mar
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: Kelvaroq takes first place: an outside tester's 36 minutes at about 10 frames a second on an RTX 4090
after.note: Kelvaroq takes first place: an outside tester's 36 minutes at about 10 frames a second on an RTX 4090  Kelvaroq's README ( 20:53 UTC ) records an outside tester's session of 36 minutes 46 seconds without a crash on an RTX 4090, through the opening mission and the next. It averaged 10 frames a second over the whole session and 10.9 after the first ten minutes, which the README describes as loading with dips to 1. It is one session, and the README says its monitor was restarted once. That gives Kelvaroq a session length where it had only 5-minute runs. It is now 2 steps short of the playable bar and takes first place from klbf-lab by the rule: the same picture step and a higher frame rate. It is the best average yet from a session of 20 minutes or more, and the first of Kelvaroq's figures from a second machine. The estimate is unchanged for now. This is the session averaging 10 or more that the published mark for moving later asked for by 12:00 UTC on 26 November , so that mark no longer applies. The mark for moving earlier asks for 12, and playable needs 20. Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 8 frames a second, with 7.2 to 7.7 standing still, and a stand-in light that follows the game's sky. Vice-Tay's README says its current build, rebuilt on VIctory's code, ran the opening cutscene at a median of 0.8 frames a second, and that its 4.3 to 7.5 came from an earlier revision.     20:40  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed
after.note: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed  PortWatch's entry for darkworldhm stood for a round and was raised at 19:59 UTC : its owner now reports free roam at 5 to 24 frames a second on the stream, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading. The build joins the table as a private row in 11th place with every figure marked as relayed. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, the code is not public, no session length is given, and nothing says whether the counter shows rendered frames. PortWatch's pinned notes since then ask the streamer to release the code. A news sweep at 20:16 UTC found no second source for that build. Coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, no notice names another project, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked. A small Manifold market, with four traders, gives about 1 in 5 that GitHub publishes a Take-Two notice naming VIctory by the end of the year. Vice-Tay's maintainer confirmed the move from victory-windows in a request on this page's repository and says the length of its test sessions is unknown. victory-perf's repository still does not answer. The estimate is unchanged. A reading of a stream is not the measured session of 10 minutes or more, averaging 12 or more in rendered frames, that the published mark asks for.      See 136 earlier updates    19:57  25 Nov

after.title: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar
after.note: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar  PortWatch removed omonkey from its board at 18:19 UTC , saying on its owner's word that the private build has been taken down. Its code was never public, so there is nothing to check, and no notice or statement has been published. VGTimes reported earlier today that its developer reported receiving a letter from Rockstar and stopped streaming. Its row here keeps its last reported status. With ztrx's repository and account gone since about 17:00 UTC , two builds of victory-fork's code have gone dark today with no reason published. The mark published with the estimate asks for a takedown notice that names VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, and GitHub's list holds none, so the estimate is unchanged. Both cases will weigh in its next review. vilocity's README now gives 4 to 8 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 3 to 7. klbf-lab's README adds that it never publishes a build that crashed in its own tests and that its 77-minute session was stopped by choice. XCL merged 28 pull requests into its main branch with its status row unchanged.     18:13  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held
after.note: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held  ztrx's repository has not answered since 16:57 UTC , in three checks over 25 minutes while every other tracked repository answered, the last of them after GitHub closed its incident at 16:52 UTC . GitHub's published list holds no notice that names it and PortWatch still lists it, so the reason is not known: a repository made private, deleted or disabled looks the same from outside. Its row keeps its last reported status, without a link. Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 7 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, from 3 to 5: 5.4 to 6.7 standing still in a scene of 8,400 draws, less while driving. Its README puts the gain down to letting the game's submissions return before the card is done and to using game memory in place instead of copying it. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it rises to 4th. BRVIctory-ka1qux has turned the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the first public build on this page to do so. Its README says it costs 0.05 to 0.1 seconds a frame and has been checked on one open-world street only, in four runs of 5 to 11 minutes without a crash. The estimate was reviewed at 17:24 UTC and held at about a day. For it: three code bases now report about 10 frames a second in early scenes, more builds and machines report every hour, and VIctory's own README says you can get into the game. after.title: A private build's developer reports a letter from Rockstar, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second
after.note: A private build's developer reports a letter from Rockstar, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second  VGTimes reports that the developer of the private build listed here as omonkey reports receiving a letter from Rockstar and has stopped streaming the work, while promising further updates. The letter has not been published and Rockstar has not commented. It is the first report of this kind seen here. Flamingo's run log reports a 24-minute play session through the whole opening and on into the city, at 8.6 frames a second on average in the world on an RTX 4070. That is the highest average reported from a session of 20 minutes or more, from one machine and unconfirmed, and it is under the 10 the next mark asks for. An open pull request against victory-fork reports the game's ray-tracing structure builder running whole through 7 minutes of play, kept off by default because it costs about 88 milliseconds a frame. VIniVIdiVIci moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5: its README reports the world at 3 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 4060 Ti, with no input tested yet. Forecast review: the estimate stays at the evening of Thu 26 Nov. The afternoon has brought more builds, a session from a new game into the open world and ray tracing as an experiment, but no figure above 14 in play, and victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC . News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no notice naming another project.     15:13  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及交互或任务；需要可重复的实机证据。

after.title: Leonida halts: its lead steps away and its repository is gone
after.note: Leonida halts: its lead steps away and its repository is gone  Leonida's lead posted a decision to step away. Its GitHub repository no longer exists at either address, its own mirror server is down, and its chat is reported gone. Whether a takedown was involved is not known. GitHub shows a notice page for repositories removed on a copyright complaint and has published none; contributors' forks and the lead's other repository are still up. The projects ahead of it are unaffected: VIctory, XCL, TuxBox and five-star-recomp were all reachable at 23:56 UTC .     23:54  23 Nov

score.note: AvatarManz's fork of VIctory, tuned for speed on an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX. It brings victory-fork's, DexNom's and Belobug's work together on VIctory and adds its own speed-ups: the game's draw calls translated on eight threads of its own, frames prepared on a separate thread, and textures uploaded on their own queue. PortWatch has verified it: GTA VI runs at about 16 fps on average in game, the highest average on our board, with sound, as far into the story as the leading builds and with a picture close to the console. Its README measures 13-22 fps indoors and on the first boat mission, and a 41-minute session without a crash.

score.note: DexNom Runtime, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon, tested on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX. after.title: AnyXboxX gives a session length and edges back to first; victory-fork reports 49 minutes of play; keylime's repository stops answering
after.note: AnyXboxX gives a session length and edges back to first; victory-fork reports 49 minutes of play; keylime's repository stops answering  AnyXboxX's README ( 22:54 UTC ) now gives a length for its figure: automated 13-minute runs on an RTX 4070 SUPER at a median of 13.8 frames a second in the world, 15.6 to 17 over the last minute, without a crash, up from 10.9 with its earlier settings. That puts the middle of its reported range just above VIctory-7900XTX's, so the two swap places, each one step short of the playable bar. victory-fork's README ( 22:50 UTC ) reports a 49-minute play session that ended when the graphics device was lost, and a later run it calls the best so far, with the water right and boats floating. It measured that nearly all of the memory it copies back from the card is read by nothing, and names that as the next thing to cut. keylime's repository stopped answering between 22:28 and 22:59 UTC : missing, private or removed. No takedown notice names it and the reason is not known. GitHub's notice list gained one entry, about an unrelated library. klbf-lab removed the names of the game, its characters and its missions from its README. vilocity reports faces lit in the opening cutscenes and a median frame of 222 milliseconds in its latest run. The estimate is unchanged: neither published mark is met.     22:39  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及权利人或平台措施；以公开原始通知为准。

after.title: VIctory-7900XTX is published with 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and goes first; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
after.note: VIctory-7900XTX is published with 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and goes first; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier  VIctory-7900XTX, a fork of VIctory whose README went up at 22:14 UTC , reports 13 to 20 frames a second indoors in the opening, 19 to 22 on the first boat mission and 6 to 10 in a busy street chase on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX at 1440p, with a longest session of 41 minutes without a crash. It gives no average for a whole session and lists flicker on trees and far buildings. PortWatch's owner says it verified the build at about 16 on average; it is one machine and nobody else has reproduced it. It enters at stage 6 in first place, one step short of the playable bar, ahead of AnyXboxX on the middle of its reported range. The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, on the mark published at 21:26 UTC , with the caveats set out in the revision note. A reader posted a 12-minute run of AnyXboxX on an RTX 4090 to this page's issues: a median of 2 frames a second in the world, rising to about 7 in its last two minutes, against the README's 12.5 on another card. The page has not verified it. AnyXboxX's speed is now marked unconfirmed, and its place still follows its own report. Vertex, a fork of VIctory measured on an RTX 5070 with 12 GB, joins at stage 6 at its maintainer's request: a median of 6.4 to 9.9 frames a second by run and a longest session of 25 minutes. after.title: VIctory merges about 70 pull requests into its main branch, vilocity clears its last orange marks and VIniVIdiVIci confirms control
after.note: VIctory merges about 70 pull requests into its main branch, vilocity clears its last orange marks and VIniVIdiVIci confirms control  VIctory's main branch took 74 commits between 21:35 and 21:57 UTC , its first since 16:51 UTC , among them the drawing of the interface planes the game uses on the smaller console's profile. Its README's status is unchanged at about 1 frame a second. vilocity's README ( 21:46 UTC ) says the last orange marks are gone, with window light and shadows now falling on heads. Its latest test run shows a median frame of 339 milliseconds, about 3 frames a second, where earlier runs showed about 130. VIniVIdiVIci's README ( 21:48 UTC ) says player control is confirmed with scripted input and nobody at the keyboard: the camera turned, the character moved and the pause menu opened. AnyXboxX has not yet given a session length for its figure of about 12 frames a second.     21:48  25 Nov
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th
after.note: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th  Vice-Tay's README ( 21:32 UTC ) reports 30 minutes 12 seconds in the world without a crash on an RTX 4090, from a save in the opening mission with the player walking and turning the camera throughout. The median over the session was 7.0 frames a second, 6.3 to 9.5 by stretch and 1.9 to 3.8 through one scene change. Its maintainer ended it by choice because memory grows by about 1 GB a minute. The row moves from 17th to 6th. VIctory's main branch took its first commits since 16:51 UTC : five merges between 21:35 and 21:40 UTC . Its README still gives about 1 frame a second. victory-fork's README ( 21:28 UTC ) says that with its new water read-back a tester's run got past a point where a mission had failed at once, then lost the graphics card for a reason not known. BRVIctory-ka1qux now gives about 3 frames a second on its street with ray-traced light and no longer lists the 6.6 to 6.9 it had reported from an earlier build.      See 140 earlier updates    21:26  25 Nov

score.note: AvatarManz's fork of VIctory, tuned for speed on an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX. It brings victory-fork's, DexNom's and Belobug's work together on VIctory and adds its own speed-ups: the game's draw calls translated on eight threads of its own, frames prepared on a separate thread, and textures uploaded on their own queue. PortWatch has verified it: GTA VI runs at about 16 fps on average in game, the highest average on our board, with sound, as far into the story as the leading builds and with a picture close to the console. Its README measures 13-22 fps indoors and on the first boat mission, and a 41-minute session without a crash.

after.title: A public fork, VIctory-NVIDIA, reports 20 to 22 frames a second indoors and joins the table; VItoriaBr moves to 3rd
after.note: A public fork, VIctory-NVIDIA, reports 20 to 22 frames a second indoors and joins the table; VItoriaBr moves to 3rd  VIctory-NVIDIA, a fork of VIctory-7900XTX made to run on NVIDIA cards, joins the table at stage 6. Its README has reported since 23:46 UTC on 25 November about 20 to 22 rendered frames a second on average indoors in the opening on an RTX 5070 with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and 24 to 31 in lighter places. This page found it only now, through a fork of it that PortWatch's scout listed. The conditions matter: the smaller console's profile, the world drawn at 960 by 540 and upscaled, ray tracing mostly off, and its fastest settings, which leave some stretched bodies and miscoloured skin. One run each in the same PC measured 19.3 on the RTX 5070 and 14.9 on an RTX 5060 Ti, and a fork measured on an RTX 4060 Ti with a Ryzen 5 5600X, now on the watch list as VKarameloVI, reports 7 to 12. Its start script is set up for a driver feature that adds generated frames, and the figures here are its rendered frames. It gives no session length, so it is on the speed step the bar asks for and 3 steps short on stability, in 11th place. It is the first public code to report an average of 20 or more in play, and with PortWatch's report on the private build CGBJ it is the second report of that kind today. The estimate, moved earlier at 04:04 UTC , is held: it already assumed a build near 20. Also: VItoriaBr's README ( 04:09 UTC ) now documents 4 to 6 frames a second on its current settings
after.analysis: 涉及运行稳定性；需要核对持续时长及是否发生崩溃。

after.title: PortWatch reports a private build, CGBJ, at 25 frames a second in gameplay; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
after.note: PortWatch reports a private build, CGBJ, at 25 frames a second in gameplay; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier  PortWatch's update of 03:58 UTC , made by a stand-in editor, says PortWatch has now seen the private build CGBJ and reports an average of 25 frames a second in gameplay on an NVIDIA card, with interiors and cutscenes near 30 and a picture it rates close to the console with minor glitches. Until now it listed the build at about 4, unlit. What the report does not give: a session length, the test machine beyond the card's maker, or whether every frame is rendered and none generated. The code is private, so nobody outside the group can test it, and PortWatch's own notes say its graphics degraded as speed improved before the rating was raised. This page relays it as unconfirmed. CGBJ's speed lane now reads 25, the first row on the step the playable bar asks for. With no session length it is still 3 steps short and moves from 28th to 8th, and VIctory-7900XTX stays first. Playable stays at no: the bar asks for 30 minutes without a crash at 20 or more, reported. The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around the evening of Thursday 26 November, UTC, with about 6 in 10 by the end of that day. The published mark asked for a session of 10 minutes or more averaging 20 with its length, which this report does not give, so the move rests on evidence the mark did not foresee and is undone if PortWatch withdraws or lowers the figure.     03:41  26 Nov

A project that reports no such session is still read from the middle of the frame rates it reports in play. Scripted or automated runs and scenes standing still do not count as play. A session average already includes such dips, and a sustained session is what the playable bar asks about. after.note: AnyXboxX reports dips to 1 to 6 frames a second while the world streams, and VIctory-7900XTX is first again  AnyXboxX's README ( 23:53 UTC ) keeps its default at about 14 to 17 frames a second, a median of 13.7 over 7 minutes, and now names its limits: a 32 GB machine is short of memory and a 12 GB card runs out of texture room, which brings dips to 1 to 6 while the world streams. A mode that favours the picture runs at about 7 to 9. With that low end the middle of the range AnyXboxX reports falls to 9, two steps short of the playable bar. VIctory-7900XTX, one step short, is first again. The two have traded first place twice since 22:39 UTC on small changes in what each reports, and a low figure is read the same way for both: a rate a project gives for a stretch or a condition of play counts, single frames do not. victory-fork's README ( 23:51 UTC ) lists new changes that are written but not yet measured in a game, one of them ported by hand from VIctory-7900XTX, and says video memory has been ruled out as the cause of its lost graphics device. On the watch list, Victory-United now reports 4.9 to 5.2 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 3080 Ti with a longest run of 8 minutes, and ScarlettCompat joins: a layer written from scratch that reports no game frame yet.     23:48  25 Nov

after.note: VIctory says only the frame rate keeps the game from working; Sixth Star joins the watch list  VIctory's README ( 23:27 UTC ) now heads its status with the frame rate as the one thing left: about 1 frame a second in the world on a Radeon RX 6700 XT, with the intro cutscene playing and the opening mission reached with the graphics fully displayed. Its figures and its place are unchanged; the faster figures on this page come from forks of its code. Sixth Star, a compatibility layer built from VIctory's code, joins the watch list at its maintainer's request. Its status file reports gameplay at about 5 frames a second on an RTX 3070 as its user's approximate observation, with stability not measured.     23:28  25 Nov

after.title: victory-fork now plays at 9 to 12 frames a second in light scenes, for half an hour at a time; VItoriaBr reports a process up for over two hours
after.note: victory-fork now plays at 9 to 12 frames a second in light scenes, for half an hour at a time; VItoriaBr reports a process up for over two hours  victory-fork's README ( 23:18 UTC ) now heads its status with play for half an hour at a time, slowly: about 9 to 12 frames a second in rooms and light outdoor views and 5 to 6 in heavy outdoor views. Its tester played from the opening past the first boat mission, and the graphics device was then lost in sessions of 6, 49 and 31 minutes, cause not known. This is the code most builds share. Its place is unchanged at 6th, two steps short: this page's playable bar asks for 20 frames a second. The README says the thread that prepares submissions is the limit, at about 70 milliseconds a frame plus 13 for every 1,000 draws. VItoriaBr's README gives one measured example of its process staying up for 2 hours 12 minutes, without saying what was played in that time. Read as its longest session, that lifts it from 22nd to 10th. News check: press coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond that notice, and GitHub's list has no new notice naming a project here. keylime's repository still does not answer.     23:05  25 Nov

after.title: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th
after.note: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th  Vice-Tay's README ( 21:32 UTC ) reports 30 minutes 12 seconds in the world without a crash on an RTX 4090, from a save in the opening mission with the player walking and turning the camera throughout. The median over the session was 7.0 frames a second, 6.3 to 9.5 by stretch and 1.9 to 3.8 through one scene change. Its maintainer ended it by choice because memory grows by about 1 GB a minute. The row moves from 17th to 6th. VIctory's main branch took its first commits since 16:51 UTC : five merges between 21:35 and 21:40 UTC . Its README still gives about 1 frame a second. victory-fork's README ( 21:28 UTC ) says that with its new water read-back a tester's run got past a point where a mission had failed at once, then lost the graphics card for a reason not known.
